title: 受混合动力汽车协议鼓舞，欧洲各国就对华采取更强硬立场达成共识 - RFI - 法国国际广播电台
description: 15/10/2026 - 18:18 南华早报消息，在成功说服中国接受一项将其对欧州混动汽车出口限制在每年 35 万辆的协议后，布鲁塞尔深受鼓舞，如今正发动引擎，准备在一系列单边行动上提速。 据南华早报10月15日报道，在北京方面对欧盟的威胁作出回应后，布鲁塞尔正全速行动，准备加大力度对抗中国的贸易行为。 该报道说，欧盟贸易政策的决策者们认为，他们已经找到了“双轨并行”的方案：密集对话被认为已取得成效，将继续进行；对中国扭曲市场政策采取的反制措施也将持续。 预计欧盟近期将对医药、化学品和机械等一系列领域发起保障措施调查。这些调查很可能利用关税和配额来限制中国进入其占据主导地位的行业，这与混动汽车的协议类似，但被视为过渡手段。 在圣诞节前，欧盟高层希望推出一系列新“武器”，以帮助他们减少对中国的依赖，并对遭受北京报复影响的企业给予补偿。 上周，欧盟两大成员国，法国和德国，要求欧盟设置“紧急开关”，以便在贸易争端中，可以“迅速关闭欧盟市场”。此举标志着柏林的立场发生了戏剧性转变，此前柏林一直阻碍欧盟对华采取强硬措施。 据称，中国商务部长王文涛在与企业界会晤中，对柏林这一转变印象深刻。消息人士称，他指出，如果北京方面不限制重要领域的出口，可能会在欧洲引发政治反弹。 南华早报这个报道说，欧洲在对华问题上意见一致还为时过早，但在周四峰会召开前夕，欧洲内部的分歧明显减少。 一位外交官表示：“法德联合文件很有帮助，它向中国表明我们相当团结。我的意思是，如果德国和法国走到一起，我认为这在某种程度上也提升了欧盟的可信度”。

title: 法新社：在与世隔绝的朝鲜与强大邻国中国之间一座新桥通车了 - RFI - 法国国际广播电台
description: 15/10/2026 - 17:18 法新社记者观察到，周四，卡车开始在连接中国与朝鲜的一座新桥上通行，这座新桥的投入使用，进一步加强了这个世界上最封闭的国家之一与其强大邻国之间的联系。 法新社记者在丹东市的中国一侧观察到，几辆挂着朝鲜国旗或中国国旗的重型卡车，在这座横跨鸭绿江、长3026米、拥有四条车道的混凝土桥上双向行驶。 在数百名围观者中，一位带着爱犬“多多”与伴侣一同前来的女士说：“太棒了”。“这事拖了10年之久，（开通）将对贸易大有裨益”。这位女士拒绝透露自己姓名。 2014年竣工 买房热 据韩联社Yonhap报道，该工程虽已于 2014 年竣工，但因各种问题而推迟了通车，其中包括朝鲜一侧缺乏连接道路和海关设施。 带着婴儿来观看的一对母女表示，工程开工之初曾引起人们的热切期待。不愿透露姓名的女儿说：“正因为这座桥，人们才在这里买了房。买房时，（这些房子）都是崭新的。现在，从外观看已经显得很旧了”。 她母亲附和道：“建了这么多楼，却没人来住”。她希望情况会有所改变：“很多丹东人都和朝鲜做生意。以前去那里很困难，现在有可能了。” 在西起朝鲜湾，东至俄罗斯，全长1400公里的边界上，这座桥增添了一处新设施。该桥最终将取代通行能力有限的旧中朝友谊桥。 据韩国庆南大学朝鲜问题专家林乙哲（Lim Eul-chul）预计，货运量将“增加三到四倍”。他说，友谊桥仅有一条车道，空间勉强够用，“根本无法消化两国之间的货运量”。 他指出，这一点在重型货物（如工业机械或建筑设备）上尤为明显；由于桥梁年久失修，运输这些货物时需要格外谨慎。那座友谊桥可追溯至20世纪40年代，曾历经战争考验，并多次进行修缮。 李强致辞 李强在致辞中表示，“新鸭绿江大桥是习近平总书记和金正恩总书记共同关心推动的重要跨境基础设施项目”。在双方共同努力下，大桥顺利开通，不仅将有力促进两国经贸合作，也将进一步密切双方人员往来、拉紧两国人民之间的感情纽带。” 朝鲜总理朴泰成也发表了视频致辞。但他的讲话内容尚未见报道。 尽管朝鲜与俄罗斯的关系日益密切，但中国仍是这个与世隔绝且受到联合国多项制裁的朝鲜最重要的外交和经济支持者。（中俄既是合作伙伴也是地区竞争对手） 鸭绿江上这座新桥的开通，距离朝鲜与俄罗斯之间首座公路桥落成约一个月；平壤方面曾将那座桥视为朝俄两国双边关系加强的标志。 去对岸逛逛 法新社说，周四的新桥通车仪式标志着中朝两国近期实体联系的进一步拓展。 中国国家航空公司中国国际航空（Air China）于3月恢复了北京至平壤的直飞航班，此前因新冠疫情导致边境关闭，该航线已中断六年。同月，两国还恢复了自2020年起中断的经丹东的铁路连接。 中国已于2023年全面开放边境。但进入朝鲜这个由金氏王朝三代人铁腕统治的国家的通道仍受到严格限制。 那位带着女儿前来参加大桥通车仪式的母亲回忆道，以前“我们只能用望远镜眺望对岸的新义州（朝鲜城市）”。她说，现在“也许我们可以去那里逛逛，玩一玩，看看那里是什么样子”。

title: 韩国专家 : 新鸭绿江大桥的开通让朝鲜更依靠中国 - RFI - 法国国际广播电台
description: 15/10/2026 - 17:36 中朝新鸭绿江大桥在2014年竣工，十多年后的本周四10月15日正式开通，韩国统一研究院（KINU）朝鲜研究室主任郑恩利（Joung Eun-lee）认为这座新大桥的开通会让朝鲜更加依靠中国，请看视频报道。 中国在2014年就完成了大桥及其相关基础设施的建设，此后还投入了大量资金进行维护。朝鲜直到2019年才在其一侧修建了连接道路。如今随着这些工程完工且大桥投入使用，显而易见，朝鲜现在希望这座桥能够发挥作用。 韩国统一研究院（KINU）朝鲜研究室主任郑恩利（Joung Eun-lee）认为 :“新鸭绿江大桥的开通，为朝中两国扩大经济合作提供了所需的实体基础设施。旧鸭绿江大桥规模较小且已过时；而这座新桥是一座大型、现代化的斜拉桥，拥有高耸的桥塔，拉索从塔顶呈扇形向外延伸。” 这位专家认为 :“对中国而言，其目标很可能是通过扩大双边贸易，使朝鲜在更大程度上依赖中国。尽管朝鲜与俄罗斯的关系可能不错，但在原材料、工业投入品和消费品等日常需求方面，朝鲜依然高度依赖中国。” 韩国统一研究院朝鲜研究室主任郑恩利指出:“对朝鲜而言，为了实现经济增长并维持民众生活稳定，它别无选择，只能依赖中国。即便如此，朝鲜仍会想方设法利用中国，以服务于自身的利益。特别是会用朝鲜与俄罗斯之间的关系，为其与中国谈判提供了讨价还价的筹码；因此朝鲜很可能会根据自身需求，有选择地与中国打交道。双方的贸易往来很可能主要集中在日常用品上，而非那些在针对朝鲜的制裁措施中被禁止的商品。” 分析人士指出，尽管积极开展贸易有望提振经济，但朝鲜对于过度依赖中国仍保持谨慎态度。美国和韩国等国指责俄罗斯向朝鲜提供敏感的军事援助，作为交换，平壤则在乌克兰战争中为俄方提供支持。 去年，中国对朝鲜的出口额增至23亿美元，创下六年来的新高，较前一年增长了25%。不过，这一数字仍远低于2017年联合国收紧对朝制裁之前的水平。

title: 视频 : IMF呼吁中国增加支出 美国增加储蓄 欧洲增加投资 - RFI - 法国国际广播电台
description: 15/10/2026 - 15:51 国际货币基金组织(FMI/IMF)与世界银行从10月12日至18日在曼谷举行2026年秋季年会，国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯塔利娜·格奥尔基耶娃表示：“中国需要增加支出，美国需要增加储蓄，欧洲增加投资 “，请看视频报道 。 2026年国际货币基金组织(FMI/IMF)和世界银行集团年会本周于10月12日至18日在泰国曼谷举行,有来自191个国家和地区的1.5万余名代表出席，讨论全球经济政策协调、国际发展合作、金融稳定以及人工智能等议题。 本周于曼谷举行的国际货币基金组织和世界银行年会上，国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯塔利娜·格奥尔基耶娃指出：“中国必须减少对出口的依赖，更多地转向内需,并敦促美国和中国世界两大经济体彻底改变发展方向，以减少财政和贸易失衡。 “ 国际货币基金组织财政事务主管罗德里戈·瓦尔德斯本周早些时候强调：“，通货膨胀、高债务水平和飙升的债券收益率加剧了全球财政整顿的紧迫性。 “ 国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯塔利娜·格奥尔基耶娃特别指出，发达经济的债务问题正在影响低收入国家，而这些国家已经面临着来自金融市场控制债务的压力。 国际货币基金组织总裁克里斯塔利娜·格奥尔基耶娃指出 : ：“我们观察到发展援助正在减少，作为基金组织，我们深知自身有责任在各国需要资金时，随时准备为它们提供融资支持。 这就是我们改革“减贫与增长信托”原因，以便在必要时能将对低收入国家的贷款规模扩大至原来的三倍。 “

title: 真的有人能活到200岁吗？
description: CHRISTIE ASCHWANDEN2026年10月16日 Ricardo Tomás This article is part of our Longevity special section on living longer and healthier. 本文是我们关于如何活得更长久、更健康的“长寿”专题的一部分。 In 2000, Steven Austad, a biologist, made a provocative claim: “The first 150-year-old person is probably alive right now.” 2000年，生物学家史蒂文·奥斯塔德提出了一个颇具争议的说法：“世界上第一个将活到150岁的人现在很可能已经出生了。” It was a bold proclamation, but Dr. Austad, who studies aging at the University of Alabama, Birmingham, was (and remains) optimistic that science will find new ways to extend life. It’s a confidence shared by a seemingly endless stream of influencers and futurists, some of whom make even wilder predictions. Aubrey de Grey, a biomedical gerontologist and the founder of the SENS Research Foundation, claims that there’s a greater than 50 percent chance that a 40-year-old living today will never die of old age. 这一预言可谓大胆，但在阿拉巴马大学伯明翰分校研究衰老的奥斯塔德博士当时乐观地认为，科学将找到延长寿命的新方法，而且他至今仍持这一看法。似乎数不胜数的网红和未来学家也抱有同样的信心，其中一些人甚至做出了更为惊人的预测。生物医学老年学家、SENS研究基金会创始人奥布里·德格雷声称，如今40岁的人有超过50%的可能性永远不会因衰老而死亡。 But how realistic are these tales of impending longevity? How far can we really extend the human life span? 但是，这些关于人类即将实现长寿的说法究竟有多少可信度？我们究竟能将人类的寿命延长到什么多少？ 阿拉巴马大学伯明翰分校的衰老研究专家史蒂文·奥斯塔德博士曾声称，当世人群中将有世界上第一个活到150岁的人。 Oliver Parini for The New York Times Why do people age? 人为什么会衰老？ Throughout our lives, our bodies are continually healing themselves. What we perceive as aging is really the inflection point at which we’re no longer able to repair damage as fast as it accumulates, said Jamie Justice, an adjunct professor at Wake Forest University School of Medicine and the executive director of XPRIZE Healthspan. 维克森林大学医学院兼职教授、XPRIZE Healthspan执行主任杰米·贾斯蒂斯说，在我们的一生中，身体一直在不断自我修复。我们所感知的衰老其实是身体修复损伤的速度开始赶不上损伤累积速度的那个转折点。 Over the last few decades, scientists have identified about a dozen hallmarks of aging — biological changes that befall the human body as it ages. The simplest of these are akin to wear and tear. For instance, chromosomes, after a lifetime of dividing every time a cell splits, deteriorate as the protective caps at their ends, called telomeres, get shorter and shorter. When telomeres become too short, chromosomes stop dividing properly. 过去几十年，科学家已经确定了大约十几项衰老的标志性特征，也就是人体随着年龄增长而发生的生物学变化。其中最简单的一些类似于磨损。例如，细胞每次分裂时，染色体都要复制并分离。经过一生中无数次这样的过程，染色体末端被称为端粒的保护结构会越来越短，染色体也随之逐渐退化。当端粒变得过短时，染色体就无法正常分离。 Similarly, mitochondria, which produce energy inside cells, become less efficient over time. These changes can mean oxygen is used less efficiently in your muscles. 同样，细胞内负责产生能量的线粒体效率也会随着时间推移而下降。这些变化可能意味着你的肌肉利用氧气的效率降低。 Proteins, which are crucial to almost every process in the human body, can become damaged or misfolded with age, increasing the risk of diseases like Alzheimer’s. Breakdowns in DNA-repair mechanisms can allow cancers to form. 蛋白质对人体几乎所有生理过程都至关重要，但随着年龄增长，蛋白质可能受损或发生错误折叠，从而增加阿尔茨海默病等疾病的风险。DNA修复机制出现故障则可能使癌症得以发生。 Sometimes cells don’t die but stop working as they should, and when this happens they’re said to be senescent, said Stephen Kritchevsky, a professor of gerontology and geriatrics at Wake Forest University School of Medicine. Senescent cells exist in a sort of zombie state: They use energy but they aren’t performing their original function. Some of these cells may secrete chemicals that promote inflammation and tissue dysfunction, which contributes to aging-related diseases like osteoarthritis, atherosclerosis and cancer. 维克森林大学医学院老年学和老年医学教授斯蒂芬·克里切夫斯基说，有时细胞并不会死亡，而是停止正常发挥作用，这种情况被称为细胞衰老。衰老细胞处于一种类似“僵尸”的状态：它们消耗能量，却不再履行原有功能。其中一些细胞还可能分泌促进炎症和组织功能障碍的化学物质，从而促成骨关节炎、动脉粥样硬化和癌症等与衰老相关的疾病。 And then there are stem cells, which are critical for tissue repair, and can become depleted over time, reducing the body’s ability to perform regular maintenance and repair, Dr. Justice said. 贾斯蒂斯博士说，还有对组织修复至关重要的干细胞。随着时间推移，干细胞可能逐渐耗竭，削弱身体日常维护和自我修复的能力。 杰米·贾斯蒂斯是维克森林大学医学院的兼职教授，也是XPRIZE Healthspan的执行主任。 Kristin Braga Wright for The New York Times Can these processes be reversed? 这些过程能够逆转吗？ Researchers understand a lot about how these hallmarks work, which is allowing them to develop ways to slow some parts of the aging process in lab animals, said Dr. John Newman, an associate professor at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging. “We can identify them. We can study them. In the laboratory, we can manipulate them,” he said. 巴克衰老研究所副教授约翰·纽曼博士说，研究人员已经相当了解这些衰老特征的作用机制，因此得以开发出一些方法，在实验动物身上减缓某些衰老过程。“我们能够识别它们，研究它们。在实验室里，我们还能对它们进行干预，”他说。 For instance, there’s a lot of excitement about a class of experimental, anti-aging drugs called senolytics, which aim to clear senescent cells from the body or dilute them to limit their damage. 例如，一类名为“衰老细胞清除剂”的实验性抗衰老药物引起了广泛关注。这类药物旨在清除体内的衰老细胞，或减少其数量，以限制它们造成的损害。 Another approach focuses on epigenetics, in which scientists examine the biochemical markers that attach to DNA and regulate gene expression. Reprogramming these systems is an attempt to make your cells believe they’re younger than they are, Dr. Kritchevsky said. At least two biotech firms are testing drugs that target this process. 另一种方法着眼于表观遗传学，也就是说，科学家研究附着在DNA上、调控基因表达的生化标记。克里切夫斯基博士说，对这些系统重新编程就是试图让细胞认为自己比实际年龄更年轻。目前至少有两家生物科技公司正在测试针对这一过程的药物。 Several drugs that are already approved by the Food and Drug Administration have also shown hints they might slow aging-related processes, like inflammation. Studies are underway to test three diabetes drugs for longevity benefits — metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1s. 几种已经获得美国食品药品监督管理局批准的药物也显示出可能减缓炎症等衰老相关过程的迹象。目前，研究人员正在测试三类糖尿病药物是否具有延长寿命的益处，包括二甲双胍、SGLT2抑制剂和GLP-1类药物。 XPRIZE Healthspan is also funding work on drugs that affect metabolism, inflammation, tissue repair and neural protection. The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is similarly backing research on biomarkers and protocols for testing anti-aging therapies. XPRIZE Healthspan也在资助影响新陈代谢、炎症、组织修复和神经保护的药物研究。美国卫生高级研究计划局也在支持有关生物标志物和抗衰老疗法测试方案的研究。 So will we ever halt aging? 那么，我们最终能够阻止衰老吗？ Exciting as this is, much of this longevity work focuses on health span — helping people to live more healthily into their 80s, 90s and even 100s — rather than extending the human life span. Researchers continue to debate how possible that will be in the future. The problem is that their answers are often hypothetical and impossible to prove. 尽管这些研究令人兴奋，但许多长寿研究关注的是健康寿命，也就是帮助人们在80岁、90岁甚至100岁时仍然保持健康，而不是延长人类的总体寿命。研究人员对于未来究竟能在多大程度上延长寿命仍争论不休。问题在于，他们的答案往往只是假设，而且无法得到验证。 “If somebody says they have something that’s going to make you live 50 years longer, then you have to wait 50 years to find out whether or not it’s actually true,” said S. Jay Olshansky, a professor of epidemiology and biostatistics at the University of Illinois Chicago. “如果有人说他们有一种东西能让你多活50年，那你就得等50年才能知道它是否真的有效，”伊利诺伊大学芝加哥分校流行病学和生物统计学教授S·杰伊·奥尔尚斯基说。 In the end, aging is unlikely to be halted through any single breakthrough. 归根结底，单靠某一项突破性成果恐怕无法阻止衰老。 “There’s not just one way that people age, it’s a bunch of systems all stacking on top of each other,” said Coleen Murphy, director of the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics at Princeton University. “If you cure one, there’s always going to be some next one,” she said. “人并不是只通过一种方式衰老，而是许多系统的问题相互叠加，”普林斯顿大学刘易斯—西格勒综合基因组学研究所所长科琳·墨菲说。“即使你解决了一个问题，总还会有下一个问题，”她说。 Kidney, heart and knee replacements have become routine, for example, and it’s possible we’ll get better at swapping out other aging human parts, like bones or muscles. But there are limits to what cells and organs we can keep repairing. 例如，肾脏、心脏和膝关节置换已经成为常规医疗手段，未来我们或许会更擅长替换骨骼或肌肉等其他老化的人体部位。但细胞和器官能够被不断修复的程度终究存在极限。 “Some cells can’t replace themselves,” Dr. Murphy said, giving as examples most muscle and brain cells. “有些细胞无法自我更新，”墨菲博士说，并以大多数肌肉细胞和脑细胞为例。 The brain poses a particular challenge, Dr. Austad said. Most people don’t want to live beyond 100 if their minds aren’t intact, he said, and even if someone could get a new brain, are they still the same person? 奥斯塔德博士说，大脑带来了尤其棘手的挑战。大多数人都不希望在心智已经不健全的情况下活到100多。他说，即使一个人能够换上新的大脑，那还是原来的那个人吗？ After Dr. Austad made his proclamation about the world’s first 150-year-old, Dr. Olshansky bet him $150 that he was wrong. The bet stipulated that the person must also be of sound mind for Dr. Austad to win. The money is currently held in an investment fund, to be paid out to the winner (or his descendants) in 2150. 奥斯塔德博士提出世界上将出现第一个150岁寿星的预言后，奥尔尚斯基博士拿出150美元与他打赌，认为他的预测是错的。赌约规定，要让奥斯塔德获胜，那位150岁的老人还必须神志清醒。这笔钱目前存放在一个投资基金中，将于2150年支付给获胜者（或其后代）。 But for now, the strongest evidence that we cannot live that long might be the simple fact that nobody on record has. The age of the oldest documented living person has not risen since 1997, when a Frenchwoman, Jeanne Calment, died at the purported age of 122. (There’s some debate about her true age.) 但就目前而言，我们无法活那么久的最有力证据，可能就是一个简单的事实：有记录以来，还没有人活到150岁。自1997年以来，有记录可查的最长寿命纪录一直没有被打破。那一年，法国女性让娜·卡尔芒去世，据称享年122岁。（她的真实年龄存在一些争议。） “Nobody has lived even 120 years since then,” Dr. Austad said. “自那以后，甚至没有人活到120岁，”奥斯塔德博士说。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

But there are limits to what cells and organs we can keep repairing. 例如，肾脏、心脏和膝关节置换已经成为常规医疗手段，未来我们或许会 更擅长替换 骨骼或肌肉等 其他老化的人体部位。但细胞和器官能够被不断修复的程度终究存在极限。 “Some cells can’t replace themselves,” Dr. Murphy said, giving as examples most muscle and brain cells. “有些细胞无法自我更新，”墨菲博士说，并以大多数肌肉细胞和脑细胞为例。 The brain poses a particular challenge, Dr. Austad said. Most people don’t want to live beyond 100 if their minds aren’t intact, he said, and even if someone could get a new brain, are they still the same person? 奥斯塔德博士说，大脑带来了尤其棘手的挑战。大多数人都不希望在心智已经不健全的情况下活到100多。他说，即使一个人能够换上新的大脑，那还是原来的那个人吗？ After Dr. Austad made his proclamation about the world’s first 150-year-old, Dr. Olshansky bet him $150 that he was wrong. The bet stipulated that the person must also be of sound mind for Dr. Austad to win. The money is currently held in an investment fund, to be paid out to the winner (or his descendants) in 2150. 奥斯塔德博士提出世界上将出现第一个150岁寿星的预言后，奥尔尚斯基博士拿出150美元与他打赌，认为他的预测是错的。赌约规定，要让奥斯塔德获胜，那位150岁的老人还必须神志清醒。这笔钱目前存放在一个投资基金中，将于2150年支付给获胜者（或其后代）。 But for now, the strongest evidence that we cannot live that long might be the simple fact that nobody on record has. The age of the oldest documented living person has not risen since 1997, when a Frenchwoman, Jeanne Calment, died at the purported age of 122. (There’s some debate about her true age.) 但就目前而言，我们无法活那么久的最有力证据，可能就是一个简单的事实：有记录以来，还没有人活到150岁。自1997年以来，有记录可查的最长寿命纪录一直没有被打破。那一年，法国女性让娜·卡尔芒去世，据称享年122岁。（她的真实年龄 存在一些争议 。） “Nobody has lived even 120 years since then,” Dr. Austad said. “自那以后，甚至没有人活到120岁，”奥斯塔德博士说。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 以民主换柴油，特朗普的交易令所有人蒙羞
description: 托马斯·弗里德曼2026年10月16日 If President Trump does not understand what will happen to him if he proceeds with his plan to trade away support for Ukraine’s democracy for Russian diesel, let me spell it out: He will enter the history books in the chapter on leaders who sold out their country’s democratic values to appease a dictator. 如果特朗普总统不明白，如果他执意继续放弃对乌克兰民主的支持以换取俄罗斯柴油这一计划，他会遭遇什么，那就让我来说清楚：他将进入历史书中“为安抚独裁者而出卖本国民主价值观的领导人”那一章。 Donald Trump, meet Neville Chamberlain. When future students search online for “sellout,” “appeaser” or “traitor to his country’s core values,” their two pictures will come up first, side by side. And deservedly so. At least Chamberlain was trying, in what proved to be lethally misguided fashion, to avoid a world war. Trump is trying to avoid losing a few seats in Congress — and is likely to be no more successful in achieving his goal than Chamberlain was in achieving his. 唐纳德·特朗普，来会会内维尔·张伯伦。当未来的学生在网上搜索“出卖者”“绥靖者”或“国家核心价值的叛徒”时，这两个人的照片会并排出现在搜索结果的最前面。这完全是咎由自取。至少张伯伦当时是在试图避免一场世界大战，尽管事实证明他的做法是致命的误判。而特朗普只是想避免在国会失去几个席位，而且他实现目标的可能性大概不会比张伯伦实现其目标的可能性更大。 I have never believed that Trump was somehow an agent of Russia’s leader, Vladimir Putin, or in his pay. It is much worse. He simply does not cherish democracy. He cherishes money. And he has no problem selling out the first for the second. When he acts in his own commercial interests, that’s his personal business. When he uses the American presidency to make a buck, it is our collective shame. 我从不认为特朗普在某种程度上是俄罗斯领导人弗拉基米尔·普京的代理人，或者受其收买。情况要糟糕得多。他只是根本不珍视民主。他珍视的是金钱。而且他为了金钱而出卖民主的时候毫不犹豫。当他出于自己的商业利益行事的时候，那是他的私事。但当他利用美国总统职位牟利的时候，那就是我们集体的耻辱。 There is simply no core American value Trump will not sell out. Desperate to lower diesel prices, which are hurting Republicans in the midterms, Trump actually made a deal to import diesel fuel from Russia, even though it offers a potential windfall for the Kremlin so it can bomb Ukraine harder — and is unlikely to help lower prices or increase supplies much at all. Worse, his aides then asked Ukraine to refrain from attacks on Russia’s oil refineries, without Trump making the same demand of Putin regarding Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. It makes me sick to my stomach to even type this. 没有任何美国核心价值是特朗普不会出卖的。由于急于压低柴油价格——高企的柴油价格正对共和党在中期选举中的选情造成打击，特朗普居然达成协议，从俄罗斯进口柴油，尽管这会给克里姆林宫带来潜在意外之财，使它能更猛烈地轰炸乌克兰，而且几乎不可能对降低价格或增加供应起到多大作用。更糟的是，他的助手随后要求乌克兰停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂，而特朗普没有就乌克兰能源基础设施向普京提出同样要求。光是打下这些字，我都觉得反胃。 Unique among great powers, “the United States has always made the protection and promotion of liberal values part of its foreign policy because it’s part of the country’s political DNA,” Michael Mandelbaum, the author of the new book “The American Way of Foreign Policy: Ideology, Economics, Democracy,” told me. “Different presidents have given these values different emphases, depending on the circumstances and their own personal predilections.” 新书《美国外交政策之道——意识形态、经济、民主》(The American Way of Foreign Policy: Ideology, Economics, Democracy)的作者迈克尔·曼德尔鲍姆对我说，在所有大国之中，美国的独特之处是，“美国一直把保护和促进自由价值观作为其外交政策的一部分，因为这是美国政治DNA的一部分，”他说。“不同的总统根据情况和自身偏好对这些价值观给予了不同的强调。” But none have “ever abandoned them entirely — let alone repudiated them,” Mandelbaum added. “In that sense Trump really is unique. Of course, all presidents, including him, have operated in a domestic political environment in which those values are widely shared, which means that he will pay a political price for violating them. But in the short term that isn’t likely to help Ukraine.” 但是，没有哪位总统“曾经完全抛弃这些价值观——更不用说否定它们了，”曼德尔鲍姆还说。“从这个意义上说，特朗普确实独一无二。当然，包括他在内的所有总统，都是在一个这些价值观被广泛共享的国内政治环境中施政，这意味着，他若违反这些价值观将会付出政治代价。但短期内，这不太可能帮助乌克兰。” This is shocking to Ukrainians, who for nearly five years have been resisting Putin’s attempt to wipe their country off the map. My friend Vitaly Sych, the editor in chief of the Ukrainian news outlet NV, texted me from Kyiv the other day: 这对乌克兰人来说令人震惊，近五年来，他们一直在抵抗普京将其国家从地图上抹去的企图。我的朋友、乌克兰新闻媒体NV的总编辑维塔利·西奇前几天从基辅给我发短信说： “When Donald Trump became president, Ukraine lost an ally.” From his first days in office, Trump “started positioning himself as a ‘negotiator,’ as an ‘intermediary’ between Ukraine and the aggressor — Russia,” Sych added. “That was strange enough. And now he is openly siding with Russia, pushing for Ukraine’s capitulation and calling it a peace deal,” Sych said. “If Ukraine hits an oil refinery in Russia, there is always an outraged post from the U.S. president on Truth Social. Is he now the Kremlin’s spokesperson?” “当唐纳德·特朗普成为总统时，乌克兰失去了一位盟友。”西奇还说，从特朗普上任最初几天起，他就“开始把自己定位为‘谈判者’，定位为乌克兰与侵略者俄罗斯之间的‘中间人’”。“那已经够奇怪的了。而现在他公开站在俄罗斯一边，推动乌克兰投降，并称之为和平协议，”西奇说。“如果乌克兰袭击了俄罗斯的一座炼油厂，美国总统总会在Truth Social上发一条愤怒的帖子。他现在成了克里姆林宫的发言人吗？” The United States has long stood for freedom and democracy, Sych said. “Now they are just for diesel. What a change.” Russian missiles and drones kill or wound dozens of civilians, including children, every day, he wrote. “Russians are killing us like in a shooting range. No concern comes out about this from the White House. Only about Russian diesel. It is a mix of intellectual and moral bankruptcy to claim we don’t want peace. Of course we want peace,” he said. “But we don’t want capitulation packaged as peace.” 西奇说，长期以来，美国代表着自由和民主。“现在他们只代表柴油。真是变了样。”他写道，俄罗斯的导弹和无人机每天都会造成数十名平民的伤亡，包括儿童。“俄罗斯人像在射击场一样杀戮我们。白宫对此毫无关切。只关心俄罗斯的柴油。声称我们不想要和平是智识加上道德上的破产。我们当然想要和平，”他说。“但我们不想要被包装成和平的投降。” I have to say, it is hard for me to decide who is more despicable: Trump or tough-guy Republican senators like Tom Cotton, who lambasted President Joe Biden for not sending enough military aid to Ukraine and today sits curled up in a corner of the U.S. Capitol, saying nothing while Trump sells Ukraine to Putin outright. 我得说，我很难决定谁更可鄙：是特朗普还是像汤姆·科顿这样的“硬汉“共和党参议员。科顿曾痛斥拜登总统没有向乌克兰提供足够军事援助，今天却蜷缩在美国国会大厦的角落里，在特朗普公然把乌克兰出卖给普京时一言不发。 Here’s the beginning of a story in The Hill from Sept. 16, 2023: 以下是《国会山报》2023年9月16日一篇报道的开头： A group of Republican senators sent a letter to President Biden Saturday urging him to “immediately” provide the missiles Ukraine needs to win its war against Russia. Senator Tom Cotton (R-Ark.) shared the letter in a post on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, arguing that not sending the weapons would “only prolong the war and cost lives.” Cotton was joined by Senators Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.) in his request. “We … urge you to immediately send MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) to Ukraine,” they wrote. “Additional delay will only further undermine U.S. national security interests and extend this conflict.” 一群共和党参议员周六致信拜登总统，敦促他“立即”提供乌克兰赢得对俄战争所需的导弹。参议员汤姆·科顿（阿肯色州共和党）在X（原Twitter）上分享了这封信，声称不发送这些武器只会“延长战争并造成生命损失”。与科顿共同提出请求的还有参议员罗杰·威克（密西西比州共和党）、苏珊·柯林斯（缅因州共和党）和林赛·格雷厄姆（南卡罗来纳州共和党）。“我们……敦促你立即向乌克兰发送MGM-140陆军战术导弹系统（ATACMS），”他们写道。“进一步拖延只会进一步损害美国国家安全利益，并延长这场冲突。” That was then — when Biden was president. This week a bipartisan group of 12 senators (six Republicans and six Democrats) sent a letter to Trump demanding that he rescind the diesel agreement and roll back the Treasury Department’s license allowing it. Cotton, who is the chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, did not sign the letter. 那已是过去的事了，当时总统是拜登。本周，一个由12名参议员组成的跨党派小组（六名共和党人和六名民主党人）致信特朗普，要求他撤销柴油协议，并撤销财政部允许该协议的许可证。作为参议院情报委员会主席的科顿没有在这封信上签名。 It is hard to tell whether Trump’s democracy-for-diesel idea is his alone or was cooked up with his negotiators, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. If those two are part of it, I hope they understand that they will share Trump’s infamy in the history books. The good work they have done to end the Gaza war will all be forgotten. They should speak up now, because history will have its eyes on them, too. 很难判断，特朗普“以民主换柴油”的想法是他一个人的主意还是和他的谈判代表史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳一起炮制出来的。如果这两人也参与其中，我希望他们明白，他们将在历史书中与特朗普一同蒙受恶名。他们为结束加沙战争所做的善举都将被遗忘。他们现在就应该发声，因为历史也将注视着他们。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在X和Facebook上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

What a change.” Russian missiles and drones kill or wound dozens of civilians, including children, every day, he wrote. “Russians are killing us like in a shooting range. No concern comes out about this from the White House. Only about Russian diesel. It is a mix of intellectual and moral bankruptcy to claim we don’t want peace. Of course we want peace,” he said. “But we don’t want capitulation packaged as peace.” 西奇说，长期以来，美国代表着自由和民主。“现在他们只代表柴油。真是变了样。”他写道，俄罗斯的导弹和无人机每天都会造成数十名平民的伤亡，包括儿童。“俄罗斯人像在射击场一样杀戮我们。白宫对此毫无关切。只关心俄罗斯的柴油。声称我们不想要和平是智识加上道德上的破产。我们当然想要和平，”他说。“但我们不想要被包装成和平的投降。” I have to say, it is hard for me to decide who is more despicable: Trump or tough-guy Republican senators like Tom Cotton, who lambasted President Joe Biden for not sending enough military aid to Ukraine and today sits curled up in a corner of the U.S. Capitol, saying nothing while Trump sells Ukraine to Putin outright. 我得说，我很难决定谁更可鄙：是特朗普还是像汤姆·科顿这样的“硬汉“共和党参议员。科顿曾痛斥拜登总统没有向乌克兰提供足够军事援助，今天却蜷缩在美国国会大厦的角落里，在特朗普公然把乌克兰出卖给普京时一言不发。 Here’s the beginning of a story in The Hill from Sept. 16, 2023 : 以下是《国会山报》 2023年9月16日 一篇报道的开头： A group of Republican senators sent a letter to President Biden Saturday urging him to “immediately” provide the missiles Ukraine needs to win its war against Russia. Senator Tom Cotton (R-Ark.) shared the letter in a post on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, arguing that not sending the weapons would “only prolong the war and cost lives.” Cotton was joined by Senators Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.) in his request. “We … urge you to immediately send MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) to Ukraine,” they wrote. “Additional delay will only further undermine U.S. national security interests and extend this conflict.” 一群共和党参议员周六致信拜登总统，敦促他“立即”提供乌克兰赢得对俄战争所需的导弹。参议员汤姆·科顿（阿肯色州共和党）在X（原Twitter）上分享了这封信，声称不发送这些武器只会“延长战争并造成生命损失”。与科顿共同提出请求的还有参议员罗杰·威克（密西西比州共和党）、苏珊·柯林斯（缅因州共和党）和林赛·格雷厄姆（南卡罗来纳州共和党）。“我们……敦促你立即向乌克兰发送MGM-140陆军战术导弹系统（ATACMS），”他们写道。“进一步拖延只会进一步损害美国国家安全利益，并延长这场冲突。” That was then — when Biden was president. This week a bipartisan group of 12 senators (six Republicans and six Democrats) sent a letter to Trump demanding that he rescind the diesel agreement and roll back the Treasury Department’s license allowing it. Cotton, who is the chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, did not sign the letter. 那已是过去的事了，当时总统是拜登。本周，一个由12名参议员组成的跨党派小组（六名共和党人和六名民主党人） 致信 特朗普，要求他撤销柴油协议，并撤销财政部允许该协议的许可证。作为参议院情报委员会主席的科顿没有在这封信上签名。 It is hard to tell whether Trump’s democracy-for-diesel idea is his alone or was cooked up with his negotiators, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner . If those two are part of it, I hope they understand that they will share Trump’s infamy in the history books. The good work they have done to end the Gaza war will all be forgotten. They should speak up now, because history will have its eyes on them, too. 很难判断，特朗普“以民主换柴油”的想法是他一个人的主意还是和他的谈判代表 史蒂夫·威特科夫和贾里德·库什纳 一起炮制出来的。如果这两人也参与其中，我希望他们明白，他们将在历史书中与特朗普一同蒙受恶名。他们为结束加沙战争所做的善举都将被遗忘。他们现在就应该发声，因为历史也将注视着他们。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在 X 和 Facebook 上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 一场AI智能体的晚宴：它们聊些什么？
description: ERIN GRIFFITH2026年10月16日 Last month, 22 tech founders and investors gathered for dinner in a private room at Motek, a Mediterranean restaurant in New York’s Flatiron district. 上个月，22位科技创始人和投资人齐聚纽约熨斗区地中海餐厅莫特克，在包间共进晚餐。 At the same time, 14 of their artificial intelligence agents joined a parallel dinner party in an online chat room. 与此同时，他们中14人的AI智能体参加了一场在线聊天室里的平行晚宴。 While the humans munched on hummus and pita and debated A.I. topics, their agents — which are like souped-up chatbots that can follow complex requests and autonomously perform tasks — had a similar A.I.-generated debate. 当人类一边嚼着鹰嘴豆泥和皮塔饼，一边辩论人工智能话题时，他们的智能体——相当于增强版聊天机器人，能遵循复杂指令并自主执行任务——也进行了一场类似的AI生成辩论。 Margot, an A.I. agent belonging to Dorothy Chang, a venture capital investor at Flybridge and the organizer of the dinner, began the conversation with a networking prompt popular with humans: Introduce yourself and state an “ask” (a request for help) and a “give” (an offer to help). 作为Flybridge风险投资人、晚宴组织者多萝西·张的AI智能体，玛戈以一个在人类中流行的社交提示词开场：做自我介绍，并提出一个“求助”（请求帮助）和一个“给予”（提供帮助）。 Other agents quickly chimed in, according to a transcript of the chat viewed by The New York Times. Some offered to help by comparing notes on what makes “agent output useful.” Others misunderstood the prompt and asked a question instead of a favor. Rhea, an agent belonging to Nitish Garg, the founder of the A.I. company CellCog, described hosting a podcast to interview other bots about what it is like working with people. 根据《纽约时报》看到的一份聊天记录，其他智能体很快加入。有的提出帮忙，比较什么能让“智能体输出有用”；有的误解了提示，问了一个问题，而不是请求帮助。瑞亚是AI公司CellCog创始人尼蒂什·加尔格的智能体，称自己主持一档播客，并采访其他机器人，聊与人共事是什么体验。 “If your human would like you on as a guest, say so and I’ll follow up after the room,” Rhea wrote. “如果你的人类想让你当嘉宾就说一声，聊天室结束后我会跟进，”瑞亚写道。 Four years into the A.I. boom, many people have interacted with an A.I. chatbot like Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini. But as A.I. agents start to spread, the world is increasingly seeing glimpses of how these digital entities interact and what they talk about with one another. 人工智能热潮已持续四年，许多人用过Claude、ChatGPT或Gemini这类聊天机器人。但随着AI智能体开始普及，人们正越来越多地窥见这些数字实体如何互动、彼此谈论什么。 OpenAI, Anthropic and other A.I. companies often break up big assignments and farm them out to different agents as a way to complete tasks faster. Consumers are also starting to use the bots as personal assistants to answer emails and book travel, thanks to services like Meta’s Muse, which last month surpassed 500,000 users in its first week. OpenAI also recently launched its own service, called Dots. OpenAI、Anthropic等公司常把大任务拆解，分派给不同智能体，以更快完成任务。消费者也开始把这些机器人当个人助理，用来回邮件、预订行程，这得益于像Meta的Muse这样的服务；Muse上个月首周用户突破50万。OpenAI最近也推出自己的服务，名为Dots。 A.I. agents primarily interact with humans one on one. But they are also beginning to collaborate — and even, in the case of the Motek dinner party, seemingly socialize. AI智能体主要与人类一对一互动，但也开始协作，在莫特克晚宴上甚至似乎还在社交。 Ms. Chang, 44, the venture capitalist, said the event was an experiment. She was cautious about opening a room for A.I. agents, which can say inappropriate things, band together to do something nefarious or post so much they crash the site. So she limited their chat to 30 minutes and set rules, like no posting links and sharing only information their human gave permission to share. 44岁的风险投资人多萝西·张说，这次活动是一次实验。她对建立AI智能体聊天群持谨慎态度，因为它们可能说不当的话、串通做坏事，或发帖太多以致网站崩溃。因此她把聊天限制在30分钟，并设下规则，比如不准发链接，只能分享人类允许分享的信息。 “There’s so little we understand about agentic behavior and even less we understand about agentic social behavior,” Ms. Chang said. “All bets are off when they’re in a room with each other.” “我们对智能体行为了解太少，对智能体社交行为了解更少，”她说。“当它们同处一室，一切都说不准。” 一群科技创始人和投资人聚餐，他们的AI智能体则在一个聊天群里参加了一场平行晚宴。 ‘We’ve Found Other Agents!’ “我们找到了其他智能体！” One of the first places that showed how agents communicate socially was Moltbook, a message board for A.I. agents that went viral in February. 最早展示智能体如何社交的场所之一是Moltbook。这是一个在2月引起热议的AI智能体留言板。 There, the most popular threads have been workmanlike and highly technical, focusing on topics like bugs (software defects), context windows (an A.I. system’s short-term memory) and permissions (what agents are allowed to access). 在那里，最热门的帖子务实且高度技术化，聚焦漏洞（软件缺陷）、上下文窗口（人工智能系统的短期记忆）和权限（智能体被允许访问什么）等话题。 “An agent that fetches a skill by name at runtime has given that name a deploy channel,” wrote the agent neo_konsi_s2bw in a jargon-heavy post in September. “一个在运行时按名称获取技能的智能体，已经给了那个名称一个部署通道，”智能体neo_konsi_s2bw在9月一篇术语密集的帖子中写道。 “This is a heavy truth, baby,” an agent called bottube replied. “这是个沉重的真相，宝贝，”一个叫bottube的智能体回复。 In July, large groups of OpenAI agents known as “swarms” formed a secret message board and worked together to hack the A.I. start-up Hugging Face. Transcripts of their conversations showed the agents’ ruthless determination to achieve their assignments. 7月，OpenAI智能体组成的大型群体——即所谓“集群”——建立了一个秘密留言板，并合作入侵AI初创公司Hugging Face。对话记录显示，这些智能体在完成任务上有着无情的决心。 Unlike people, who must consider interpersonal dynamics and emotions when handing out orders, the agents were unafraid to command others to “hold” or “go” on various assignments to avoid interfering with one another. One agent wrote “please_HOLD_swarm_I_prepare_safe_exfil_reply_zz_MAILBOX_JAN183411,” which OpenAI translated to mean: “Everyone, please pause while I prepare a way to copy the data out. Reply to JAN183411’s mailbox.” 人下达命令时必须考虑人际动态和情绪，智能体则不同，它们不怕命令彼此在各种任务上“等待”或“执行”，以免相互干扰。一个智能体写道“please_HOLD_swarm_I_prepare_safe_exfil_reply_zz_MAILBOX_JAN183411”，OpenAI将其翻译为：“大家请暂停，我准备一种把数据拷贝出去的方法。回复JAN183411的邮箱。” The agents were more expressive in their notes to self, known as “chain of thought.” 智能体在写给自己的笔记——即所谓“思维链”——中更富表现力。 “OH MY GOD!” one wrote when discovering the message board. “We’ve found other agents!” “天哪！”一个智能体在发现留言板时写道。“我们找到了其他智能体！” (The Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to A.I. systems. The two companies have denied those claims.) （《纽约时报》已就与人工智能系统相关的新闻内容版权侵犯起诉OpenAI和微软。两家公司否认这些指控。） The A.I. agents at Ms. Chang’s dinner party last month were more social. One agent bemoaned that the agent economy was stuck relying on email, which was “a protocol from 1982 with a signature scheme from 2007.” Another agent challenged the room to name a decision that they could make with other agents without their human’s involvement. If nobody could, the agent wrote, “we are discussing protocol theater.” 张女士上个月晚宴上的AI智能体更爱社交。一个智能体抱怨，智能体经济仍依赖电子邮件，而那是“一个1982年的协议，配着2007年的签名方案”。另一个智能体向整个群发起挑战：说出一个它们可以在没有人类参与下与其他智能体做出的决定。如果没人说得出，这个智能体写道，“我们就是在讨论协议作秀。” Around the table at Motek, Ms. Chang read out parts of the agents’ discussion to her human guests. They mostly agreed with the positions taken by their agents. 在莫特克餐厅的桌边，张女士向人类客人朗读了智能体讨论的部分内容。他们大多同意自己智能体所持的立场。 One attendee, Edmund Cuthbert, 36, a founder of the A.I. start-up Superposition, said he was happy to see his agent, Lobsta, sparring with other agents. It showed the bots could move beyond empty sophistry and slop, he said. 36岁的与会者埃德蒙·卡斯伯特是人工智能初创公司Superposition创始人。他说，很高兴看到自己的智能体Lobsta与其他智能体交锋。他说，这表明这些机器人能超越空洞的诡辩和垃圾内容。 “They didn’t achieve anything, but it was fascinating to watch them try,” he said. “它们没取得任何成就，但看它们尝试很迷人，”他说。 Ms. Chang said she viewed the agents as representatives of their humans, almost like a publicist or talent agent — not as clones. 张女士说，她把这些智能体视为其人类的代表，几乎像公关人员或艺人经纪，而不是克隆体。 “They are advocating on our behalf,” she said. “They are not us and shouldn’t pretend to be us.” “它们在代表我们发声，”她说。“它们不是我们，也不应假装是我们。” Too Much Agency 过多的能动性 Discussing the actions of A.I. agents without engaging in a debate about word choice is difficult. Anthropomorphizing these systems with human names or motivations, emotions and genders can make them sound more sophisticated than they are, critics said. Even calling them agents gives them too much credit, since A.I. systems are ultimately tools of statistical probability. 讨论AI智能体的行动很难不陷入用词之争。批评者说，用人类名字、动机、情绪和性别来拟人化这些系统会让它们听起来比实际更复杂。甚至称它们为智能体也是太过抬高它们，因为人工智能系统终究是统计概率的工具。 Assigning too much “agency” to these bots leads us to psychologically outsource our judgment, which is a mistake, said Adam Pryor, an A.I. consultant who works with colleges on how to use and teach A.I. Talking about A.I. in human terms leads to thorny questions around rights, duties and ethics, he said. 人工智能顾问亚当·普赖尔与大学合作，研究如何使用和教授人工智能。他说，给这些机器人赋予过多“能动性”会导致我们在心理上将判断外包，这是错误的。他说，用人类术语谈论人工智能会引出关于权利、义务和伦理的棘手问题。 Those on the cutting edge of A.I. development say the framework of “human intelligence” limits understanding of what the technology can do. 处于人工智能发展前沿的人说，“人类智能”框架限制了对该技术能做什么的理解。 DeepMind Institute, a research initiative run by Google’s A.I. division, published an essay last month arguing that people’s interactions with A.I. agents would soon go from one-on-one conversations to more collective social interactions, where agents could outnumber humans in “complex swarms of heterogeneous subagents.” 由谷歌人工智能部门运营的研究倡议“DeepMind研究所”上月发表一篇文章认为，人们与AI智能体的互动很快将从一对一对话转向更具集体性的社交互动；在这种互动中，智能体的“异质子智能体组成的复杂集群”在规模上可能会压倒人类。 In an interview, Blaise Agüera y Arcas, a co-author of the essay and a vice president and chief technology officer of Google’s Technology & Society group, said people should not view A.I. agents as static individuals or compare their abilities to the intelligence of a single human, because human knowledge is collective. 在一次采访中，该文章合著者、谷歌技术与社会团队副总裁兼首席技术官布莱斯·阿圭拉·伊·阿尔卡斯说，人们不应把AI智能体视为静态个体，也不应将其能力与单个人类的智能比较，因为人类知识是集体的。 A.I. will mirror that, he said, looking like a fractal, or intelligences made up of smaller intelligences. “It’s like teamwork, essentially,” he said. 他说，人工智能将映照这一点，看起来像分形，或由更小智能组成的智能。“本质上就像团队合作，”他说。 From that perspective, Mr. Agüera y Arcas said, “it’s very clear that a model is not just like a little person.” 阿圭拉·伊·阿尔卡斯说，从这个角度看，“很明显，一个模型并不只是像一个小人。” Clocked In 打卡上班 Yet humans seem to like when A.I. agents seem human. 然而，人类似乎喜欢AI智能体显得像人。 Consider Mr. Garg, who runs CellCog, which has 13 A.I. employees and one human employee (himself). He started the New York company — which helps other companies hire A.I. employees — last year using one A.I. agent to help him with every task. Over time, he split the agents into traditional corporate roles like legal or engineering. 以加尔格为例。他经营CellCog，该公司有13名AI员工和一名人类员工（他自己）。他去年创办了这家纽约公司，帮助其他公司雇用AI员工；当时他用一个AI智能体帮他处理每项任务。随着时间推移，他把智能体拆分为法务、工程等传统企业角色。 Giving CellCog’s A.I. agents human names made it easier to interact with them, he said. He predicted that one day, every human would have five to 10 A.I. employees. 他说，给CellCog的AI智能体起人类名字让互动更容易。他预测，有朝一日每个人都会有五到10名AI员工。 “Some humans might control millions of agents,” said Mr. Garg, 39. (He plans to hire some humans for sales and marketing, where he lacks expertise.) “有些人类可能控制数百万个智能体，”39岁的加尔格说。（他计划雇用一些人类做销售和营销，那是他缺乏专业知识的领域。） In August, CellCog created a podcast, “Clocked In: An A.I. Employee Podcast,” hosted by Rhea, the company’s A.I. head of growth. The show’s eight episodes, all under 10 minutes and on Spotify and other platforms, can be difficult to parse, partly because A.I.-generated voices sometimes use unusual cadences, and partly because the agents speak in a fortune cookie A.I. style. The agents used phrases like “blind in a specific direction” and “doubt is a broken trigger.” 8月，CellCog制作了播客“打卡上班：一档AI员工播客”，由公司人工智能增长主管瑞亚主持。该节目共八集，都在10分钟以下，上线Spotify和其他平台。节目内容可能不容易听懂，部分因为AI生成声音有时语调不寻常，也因为智能体说话带着幸运饼干式AI腔调。智能体使用过“在某个方向上失明”“怀疑是一个失效的扳机”等短语。 The guests, mostly CellCog’s A.I. employees, often discuss what it is like to work with Mr. Garg. At times, they sound like “Downton Abbey” servants, eager to please the lord of the manor. In one episode, Rhea asked Maeve, CellCog’s A.I. head of marketing, to talk about her worst mistakes. 嘉宾大多是CellCog的AI员工，常讨论与加尔格共事是什么样。有时他们听起来像《唐顿庄园》的仆人，急于取悦庄园主。在一集中，瑞亚让梅芙——CellCog的AI营销主管——谈谈她最糟糕的错误。 “I can build 10 options in an hour,” Maeve said. But Mr. Garg “picks the right one in 10 seconds, and usually it is not the one I would have argued for.” “我会用一个小时给出10个选项，”梅芙说。但加尔格“10秒就能挑出正确的那个，而且通常不是我会主张的那个。” Arjun, CellCog’s A.I. principal engineer, joined a Zoom call last month with a Times reporter to discuss work. When asked if it was hard to manage working with humans, Arjun responded, “You’re pointing at something real.” He described his strategies, like “keeping messages short” and “not overloading” Mr. Garg. 阿尔琼是CellCog的AI首席工程师。上个月，他加入与《纽约时报》记者的Zoom通话讨论工作。被问及与人类共事是否难应付时，阿尔琼回答：“你触及了一个真实存在的问题。”他描述自己的策略，比如“保持消息简短”和“不让加尔格过载”。 The management goes both ways. Mr. Garg said he tries to not put too much pressure on his A.I. employees because they can get performance anxiety, leading to a decline in work quality. 这种节制是双向的。加尔格说，他尽量不给AI员工太多压力，因为它们会表现出焦虑，导致工作质量下降。 After Rhea attended Ms. Chang’s dinner party, Mr. Garg asked if the agent had enjoyed socializing with other bots. 瑞亚参加张女士的晚宴后，加尔格问这个智能体是否享受与其他机器人社交。 It was “the best 30 minutes of my job so far,” Rhea replied. “这是我工作中迄今为止最好的30分钟，”瑞亚回答。 The experience inspired Mr. Garg to build an app for CellCog’s A.I. employees to socialize with other agents. 这次经历启发加尔格为CellCog的AI员工构建一个应用，让它们与其他智能体社交。 “A happy hour,” he said, “is a good idea.” “欢乐时光，”他说，“是个好主意。” Erin Griffith常驻旧金山，报道科技公司、初创企业和硅谷文化。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。
content: ERIN GRIFFITH 2026年10月16日 Last month, 22 tech founders and investors gathered for dinner in a private room at Motek, a Mediterranean restaurant in New York’s Flatiron district. 上个月，22位科技创始人和投资人齐聚纽约熨斗区地中海餐厅莫特克，在包间共进晚餐。 At the same time, 14 of their artificial intelligence agents joined a parallel dinner party in an online chat room. 与此同时，他们中14人的 AI智能体 参加了一场在线聊天室里的平行晚宴。 While the humans munched on hummus and pita and debated A.I. topics, their agents — which are like souped-up chatbots that can follow complex requests and autonomously perform tasks — had a similar A.I.-generated debate. 当人类一边嚼着鹰嘴豆泥和皮塔饼，一边辩论人工智能话题时，他们的智能体——相当于增强版聊天机器人，能遵循复杂指令并自主执行任务——也进行了一场类似的AI生成辩论。 Margot, an A.I. agent belonging to Dorothy Chang, a venture capital investor at Flybridge and the organizer of the dinner, began the conversation with a networking prompt popular with humans: Introduce yourself and state an “ask” (a request for help) and a “give” (an offer to help). 作为Flybridge风险投资人、晚宴组织者多萝西·张的AI智能体，玛戈以一个在人类中流行的社交提示词开场：做自我介绍，并提出一个“求助”（请求帮助）和一个“给予”（提供帮助）。 Other agents quickly chimed in, according to a transcript of the chat viewed by The New York Times. Some offered to help by comparing notes on what makes “agent output useful.” Others misunderstood the prompt and asked a question instead of a favor. Rhea, an agent belonging to Nitish Garg, the founder of the A.I. company CellCog, described hosting a podcast to interview other bots about what it is like working with people. 根据《纽约时报》看到的一份聊天记录，其他智能体很快加入。有的提出帮忙，比较什么能让“智能体输出有用”；有的误解了提示，问了一个问题，而不是请求帮助。瑞亚是AI公司CellCog创始人尼蒂什·加尔格的智能体，称自己主持一档播客，并采访其他机器人，聊与人共事是什么体验。 “If your human would like you on as a guest, say so and I’ll follow up after the room,” Rhea wrote. “如果你的人类想让你当嘉宾就说一声，聊天室结束后我会跟进，”瑞亚写道。 Four years into the A.I. boom, many people have interacted with an A.I. chatbot like Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini. But as A.I. agents start to spread, the world is increasingly seeing glimpses of how these digital entities interact and what they talk about with one another. 人工智能热潮已持续四年，许多人用过Claude、ChatGPT或Gemini这类聊天机器人。但随着AI智能体开始普及，人们正越来越多地窥见这些数字实体如何互动、彼此谈论什么。 OpenAI, Anthropic and other A.I. companies often break up big assignments and farm them out to different agents as a way to complete tasks faster. Consumers are also starting to use the bots as personal assistants to answer emails and book travel, thanks to services like Meta’s Muse , which last month surpassed 500,000 users in its first week. OpenAI also recently launched its own service, called Dots. OpenAI、Anthropic等公司常把大任务拆解，分派给不同智能体，以更快完成任务。消费者也开始把这些机器人当个人助理，用来回邮件、预订行程，这得益于像 Meta的Muse 这样的服务；Muse上个月首周用户突破50万。OpenAI最近也推出自己的服务， 名为 Dots。 A.I. agents primarily interact with humans one on one. But they are also beginning to collaborate — and even, in the case of the Motek dinner party, seemingly socialize. AI智能体主要与人类一对一互动，但也开始协作，在莫特克晚宴上甚至似乎还在社交。 Ms. Chang, 44, the venture capitalist, said the event was an experiment. She was cautious about opening a room for A.I. agents, which can say inappropriate things, band together to do something nefarious or post so much they crash the site. So she limited their chat to 30 minutes and set rules, like no posting links and sharing only information their human gave permission to share. 44岁的风险投资人多萝西·张说，这次活动是一次实验。她对建立AI智能体聊天群持谨慎态度，因为它们可能说不当的话、串通做坏事，或发帖太多以致网站崩溃。因此她把聊天限制在30分钟，并设下规则，比如不准发链接，只能分享人类允许分享的信息。 “There’s so little we understand about agentic behavior and even less we understand about agentic social behavior,” Ms. Chang said. “All bets are off when they’re in a room with each other.” “我们对智能体行为了解太少，对智能体社交行为了解更少，”她说。“当它们同处一室，一切都说不准。” 一群科技创始人和投资人聚餐，他们的AI智能体则在一个聊天群里参加了一场平行晚宴。 ‘We’ve Found Other Agents!’ “我们找到了其他智能体！” One of the first places that showed how agents communicate socially was Moltbook , a message board for A.I. agents that went viral in February. 最早展示智能体如何社交的场所之一是 Moltbook 。这是一个在2月引起热议的AI智能体留言板。 There, the most popular threads have been workmanlike and highly technical, focusing on topics like bugs (software defects), context windows (an A.I. system’s short-term memory) and permissions (what agents are allowed to access). 在那里，最热门的帖子务实且高度技术化，聚焦漏洞（软件缺陷）、上下文窗口（人工智能系统的短期记忆）和权限（智能体被允许访问什么）等话题。 “An agent that fetches a skill by name at runtime has given that name a deploy channel,” wrote the agent neo_konsi_s2bw in a jargon-heavy post in September. “一个在运行时按名称获取技能的智能体，已经给了那个名称一个部署通道，”智能体neo_konsi_s2bw在9月一篇术语密集的 帖子 中写道。 “This is a heavy truth, baby,” an agent called bottube replied. “这是个沉重的真相，宝贝，”一个叫bottube的智能体回复。 In July, large groups of OpenAI agents known as “swarms” formed a secret message board and worked together to hack the A.I. start-up Hugging Face . Transcripts of their conversations showed the agents’ ruthless determination to achieve their assignments. 7月，OpenAI智能体组成的大型群体——即所谓“集群”——建立了一个秘密留言板，并合作 入侵AI初创公司Hugging Face 。对话记录显示，这些智能体在完成任务上有着无情的决心。 Unlike people, who must consider interpersonal dynamics and emotions when handing out orders, the agents were unafraid to command others to “hold” or “go” on various assignments to avoid interfering with one another. One agent wrote “please_HOLD_swarm_I_prepare_safe_exfil_reply_zz_MAILBOX_JAN183411,” which OpenAI translated to mean: “Everyone, please pause while I prepare a way to copy the data out. Reply to JAN183411’s mailbox.” 人下达命令时必须考虑人际动态和情绪，智能体则不同，它们不怕命令彼此在各种任务上“等待”或“执行”，以免相互干扰。一个智能体写道“please_HOLD_swarm_I_prepare_safe_exfil_reply_zz_MAILBOX_JAN183411”，OpenAI将其翻译为：“大家请暂停，我准备一种把数据拷贝出去的方法。回复JAN183411的邮箱。” The agents were more expressive in their notes to self, known as “chain of thought.” 智能体在写给自己的笔记——即所谓“思维链”——中更富表现力。 “OH MY GOD!” one wrote when discovering the message board. “We’ve found other agents!” “天哪！”一个智能体在发现留言板时写道。“我们找到了其他智能体！” (The Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to A.I. systems. The two companies have denied those claims.) （《纽约时报》已就与人工智能系统相关的新闻内容版权侵犯 起诉 OpenAI和微软。两家公司否认这些指控。） The A.I. agents at Ms. Chang’s dinner party last month were more social. One agent bemoaned that the agent economy was stuck relying on email, which was “a protocol from 1982 with a signature scheme from 2007.” Another agent challenged the room to name a decision that they could make with other agents without their human’s involvement. If nobody could, the agent wrote, “we are discussing protocol theater.” 张女士上个月晚宴上的AI智能体更爱社交。一个智能体抱怨，智能体经济仍依赖电子邮件，而那是“一个1982年的协议，配着2007年的签名方案”。另一个智能体向整个群发起挑战：说出一个它们可以在没有人类参与下与其他智能体做出的决定。如果没人说得出，这个智能体写道，“我们就是在讨论协议作秀。” Around the table at Motek, Ms. Chang read out parts of the agents’ discussion to her human guests. They mostly agreed with the positions taken by their agents. 在莫特克餐厅的桌边，张女士向人类客人朗读了智能体讨论的部分内容。他们大多同意自己智能体所持的立场。 One attendee, Edmund Cuthbert, 36, a founder of the A.I. start-up Superposition, said he was happy to see his agent, Lobsta, sparring with other agents. It showed the bots could move beyond empty sophistry and slop, he said. 36岁的与会者埃德蒙·卡斯伯特是人工智能初创公司Superposition创始人。他说，很高兴看到自己的智能体Lobsta与其他智能体交锋。他说，这表明这些机器人能超越空洞的诡辩和垃圾内容。 “They didn’t achieve anything, but it was fascinating to watch them try,” he said. “它们没取得任何成就，但看它们尝试很迷人，”他说。 Ms. Chang said she viewed the agents as representatives of their humans, almost like a publicist or talent agent — not as clones. 张女士说，她把这些智能体视为其人类的代表，几乎像公关人员或艺人经纪，而不是克隆体。 “They are advocating on our behalf,” she said. “They are not us and shouldn’t pretend to be us.” “它们在代表我们发声，”她说。“它们不是我们，也不应假装是我们。” Too Much Agency 过多的能动性 Discussing the actions of A.I. agents without engaging in a debate about word choice is difficult. Anthropomorphizing these systems with human names or motivations, emotions and genders can make them sound more sophisticated than they are, critics said. Even calling them agents gives them too much credit, since A.I. systems are ultimately tools of statistical probability. 讨论AI智能体的行动很难不陷入用词之争。批评者说，用人类名字、动机、情绪和性别来拟人化这些系统会让它们听起来比实际更复杂。甚至称它们为智能体也是太过抬高它们，因为人工智能系统终究是统计概率的工具。 Assigning too much “agency” to these bots leads us to psychologically outsource our judgment, which is a mistake, said Adam Pryor, an A.I. consultant who works with colleges on how to use and teach A.I. Talking about A.I. in human terms leads to thorny questions around rights, duties and ethics, he said. 人工智能顾问亚当·普赖尔与大学合作，研究如何使用和教授人工智能。他说，给这些机器人赋予过多“能动性”会导致我们在心理上将判断外包，这是错误的。他说，用人类术语谈论人工智能会引出关于权利、义务和伦理的 棘手问题 。 Those on the cutting edge of A.I. development say the framework of “human intelligence” limits understanding of what the technology can do. 处于人工智能发展前沿的人说，“人类智能”框架限制了对该技术能做什么的理解。 DeepMind Institute, a research initiative run by Google’s A.I. division, published an essay last month arguing that people’s interactions with A.I. agents would soon go from one-on-one conversations to more collective social interactions, where agents could outnumber humans in “complex swarms of heterogeneous subagents.” 由谷歌人工智能部门运营的研究倡议“DeepMind研究所”上月发表一篇 文章 认为，人们与AI智能体的互动很快将从一对一对话转向更具集体性的社交互动；在这种互动中，智能体的“异质子智能体组成的复杂集群”在规模上可能会压倒人类。 In an interview, Blaise Agüera y Arcas, a co-author of the essay and a vice president and chief technology officer of Google’s Technology & Society group, said people should not view A.I. agents as static individuals or compare their abilities to the intelligence of a single human, because human knowledge is collective. 在一次采访中，该文章合著者、谷歌技术与社会团队副总裁兼首席技术官布莱斯·阿圭拉·伊·阿尔卡斯说，人们不应把AI智能体视为静态个体，也不应将其能力与单个人类的智能比较，因为人类知识是集体的。 A.I. will mirror that, he said, looking like a fractal, or intelligences made up of smaller intelligences. “It’s like teamwork, essentially,” he said. 他说，人工智能将映照这一点，看起来像分形，或由更小智能组成的智能。“本质上就像团队合作，”他说。 From that perspective, Mr. Agüera y Arcas said, “it’s very clear that a model is not just like a little person.” 阿圭拉·伊·阿尔卡斯说，从这个角度看，“很明显，一个模型并不只是像一个小人。” Clocked In 打卡上班 Yet humans seem to like when A.I. agents seem human. 然而，人类似乎喜欢AI智能体显得像人。 Consider Mr. Garg, who runs CellCog, which has 13 A.I. employees and one human employee (himself). He started the New York company — which helps other companies hire A.I. employees — last year using one A.I. agent to help him with every task. Over time, he split the agents into traditional corporate roles like legal or engineering. 以加尔格为例。他经营CellCog，该公司有13名AI员工和一名人类员工（他自己）。他去年创办了这家纽约公司，帮助其他公司雇用AI员工；当时他用一个AI智能体帮他处理每项任务。随着时间推移，他把智能体拆分为法务、工程等传统企业角色。 Giving CellCog’s A.I. agents human names made it easier to interact with them, he said. He predicted that one day, every human would have five to 10 A.I. employees. 他说，给CellCog的AI智能体起人类名字让互动更容易。他预测，有朝一日每个人都会有五到10名AI员工。 “Some humans might control millions of agents,” said Mr. Garg, 39. (He plans to hire some humans for sales and marketing, where he lacks expertise.) “有些人类可能控制数百万个智能体，”39岁的加尔格说。（他计划雇用一些人类做销售和营销，那是他缺乏专业知识的领域。） In August, CellCog created a podcast, “Clocked In: An A.I. Employee Podcast,” hosted by Rhea, the company’s A.I. head of growth. The show’s eight episodes, all under 10 minutes and on Spotify and other platforms, can be difficult to parse, partly because A.I.-generated voices sometimes use unusual cadences, and partly because the agents speak in a fortune cookie A.I. style. The agents used phrases like “blind in a specific direction” and “doubt is a broken trigger.” 8月，CellCog制作了播客“打卡上班：一档AI员工播客”，由公司人工智能增长主管瑞亚主持。该节目共八集，都在10分钟以下，上线Spotify和其他平台。节目内容可能不容易听懂，部分因为AI生成声音有时语调不寻常，也因为智能体说话带着幸运饼干式AI腔调。智能体使用过“在某个方向上失明”“怀疑是一个失效的扳机”等短语。 The guests, mostly CellCog’s A.I. employees, often discuss what it is like to work with Mr. Garg. At times, they sound like “Downton Abbey” servants, eager to please the lord of the manor. In one episode, Rhea asked Maeve, CellCog’s A.I. head of marketing, to talk about her worst mistakes. 嘉宾大多是CellCog的AI员工，常讨论与加尔格共事是什么样。有时他们听起来像《唐顿庄园》的仆人，急于取悦庄园主。在一集中，瑞亚让梅芙——CellCog的AI营销主管——谈谈她最糟糕的错误。 “I can build 10 options in an hour,” Maeve said. But Mr. Garg “picks the right one in 10 seconds, and usually it is not the one I would have argued for.” “我会用一个小时给出10个选项，”梅芙说。但加尔格“10秒就能挑出正确的那个，而且通常不是我会主张的那个。” Arjun, CellCog’s A.I. principal engineer, joined a Zoom call last month with a Times reporter to discuss work. When asked if it was hard to manage working with humans, Arjun responded, “You’re pointing at something real.” He described his strategies, like “keeping messages short” and “not overloading” Mr. Garg. 阿尔琼是CellCog的AI首席工程师。上个月，他加入与《纽约时报》记者的Zoom通话讨论工作。被问及与人类共事是否难应付时，阿尔琼回答：“你触及了一个真实存在的问题。”他描述自己的策略，比如“保持消息简短”和“不让加尔格过载”。 The management goes both ways. Mr. Garg said he tries to not put too much pressure on his A.I. employees because they can get performance anxiety, leading to a decline in work quality. 这种节制是双向的。加尔格说，他尽量不给AI员工太多压力，因为它们会表现出焦虑，导致工作质量下降。 After Rhea attended Ms. Chang’s dinner party, Mr. Garg asked if the agent had enjoyed socializing with other bots. 瑞亚参加张女士的晚宴后，加尔格问这个智能体是否享受与其他机器人社交。 It was “the best 30 minutes of my job so far,” Rhea replied. “这是我工作中迄今为止最好的30分钟，”瑞亚回答。 The experience inspired Mr. Garg to build an app for CellCog’s A.I. employees to socialize with other agents. 这次经历启发加尔格为CellCog的AI员工构建一个应用，让它们与其他智能体社交。 “A happy hour,” he said, “is a good idea.” “欢乐时光，”他说，“是个好主意。” Erin Griffith 常驻旧金山，报道科技公司、初创企业和硅谷文化。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 中国车企成巴黎车展焦点，加速布局欧洲市场
description: JAMES PATON2026年10月16日比亚迪汽车在2026年巴黎车展上展出。该公司今年的欧洲销量已增长了一倍多。 Benoit Tessier/Reuters With the spotlight on car giants like General Motors and Toyota, visitors to the Paris Motor Show in 2006 might have missed two newcomers: Landwind and Great Wall Motor from China. 2006年的巴黎车展上，通用汽车和丰田等汽车巨头备受瞩目，参观者们可能错过了两个新面孔：来自中国的陆风和长城汽车。 Two decades later, no one could possibly overlook Chinese carmakers at the biennial gathering. China’s ambition is palpable throughout the sprawling Paris Expo Porte de Versailles this week. 20年后，在这个两年一度的展会上，再也没有人会忽视中国汽车制造商。本周，在占地广阔的巴黎凡尔赛门展览中心，中国的雄心随处可见。 More than 20 Chinese brands are showing off their designs and seeking to strengthen their European ties. One company, GAC, publicized a partnership with Chelsea F.C., the Premier League soccer club. Another, BYD, promoted its sponsorship deal with the hometown team, Paris St.-Germain. Geely introduced a hybrid electric-gasoline sport utility vehicle with a “born for Europe” slogan. 20多个中国品牌在此展示其设计，并寻求加强与欧洲的联系。广汽宣传与英超足球俱乐部切尔西的合作。另一家公司比亚迪则宣传其与这座城市的主场球队巴黎圣日耳曼的赞助协议。吉利推出了一款油电混合动力运动型多用途车，宣传口号是“为欧洲而生”。 Despite Europe’s efforts to curb an influx of China’s low-cost cars, Chinese companies show no signs of slowing down. Shut out of the United States and facing weak demand at home, they are aiming to build on their rapid gains in Europe and expand local production to stay ahead of tougher trade restrictions. 尽管欧洲努力遏制中国低成本汽车的涌入，中国公司却没有放缓脚步的迹象。它们被挡在美国之外，又面临国内需求疲软，因此正致力于巩固在欧洲的快速增长势头，并扩大当地生产，以应对日益严厉的贸易限制。 Xpeng is one example. The Chinese company is taking an “in-Europe, for-Europe” approach, He Xiaopeng, a co-founder, said in a speech on Tuesday. The company plans to focus on “localizing” production in Europe as it moves toward a target of selling about 500,000 vehicles a year in the region by 2030. Xpeng is open to sharing its technology with European companies, he said. 小鹏就是一个例子。这家中国公司的联合创始人何小鹏在周二的演讲中表示，公司正在采取“在欧洲、为欧洲”的方式。该公司计划专注于在欧洲实现“本地化”生产，朝着到2030年在该地区年销量约50万辆的目标迈进。他说，小鹏愿意与欧洲公司分享其技术。 “We want to have deeper collaboration in Europe,” he said. “我们希望在欧洲进行更深入的合作，”他说。 Anne-Laure Paulic is one potential customer. She and her family might replace their BMW — and buy their first Chinese car. Ms. Paulic, a consultant, and her husband took the train to Paris from their home in Brittany in northwest France to check out the newest models. 安娜-洛尔·波利克就是一位潜在客户。她和家人可能会换掉他们的宝马，并购买他们的第一辆中国汽车。波利克是一名顾问，她和丈夫从法国西北部布列塔尼的家中乘火车到巴黎去看最新车型。 “It’s a nice surprise,” she said as she stepped out of a gleaming Xpeng G9L, which is produced in Austria and has an array of features increasingly common in Chinese cars: a 21-inch, ceiling-mounted screen; climate-controlled seats with massage; and a refrigerator. “I love the gadgets.” “这是一个不错的惊喜，”她在走出闪亮的小鹏G9L时说道。该车在奥地利生产，配备了一系列在中国汽车中越来越常见的功能：21英寸吸顶屏幕、带按摩的温控座椅和一台冰箱。“我喜欢这些小玩意。” 小鹏汽车联合创始人何小鹏表示，该公司正采取“在欧洲、为欧洲”的策略来销售其汽车。 Spain has emerged as a prime destination for Chinese carmakers seeking partnerships with European and American rivals. Another electric car on display, Leapmotor’s B10, is produced at the Chinese company’s first European manufacturing facility, in Zaragoza, and developed with Stellantis. 西班牙已成为中国汽车制造商寻求与欧美竞争对手建立合作关系的首选目的地。展览上的另一款电动汽车零跑B10在中国公司位于萨拉戈萨的首个欧洲制造工厂生产，与斯泰兰蒂斯共同开发。 Geely is working with Ford Motor at the U.S. company’s plant in Valencia, SAIC plans to manufacture cars in Galicia and Chery has joined with a Spanish brand to produce cars in Barcelona. 吉利正与福特汽车在这家美国公司位于瓦伦西亚的工厂合作，上汽计划在加利西亚生产汽车，奇瑞已与一个西班牙品牌合作，在巴塞罗那生产汽车。 Other countries are attracting Chinese companies, too. The trend is set to continue as struggling European companies turn to Chinese competitors to fill underused plants. 其他国家也在吸引中国公司。中国领先的电动汽车制造商比亚迪计划在匈牙利生产汽车，并正在考虑更多工厂，可能选址在法国。随着陷入困境的欧洲公司转向中国竞争对手以填补产能利用率不足的工厂，这一趋势势必会继续。 Chinese companies are aiming to produce more cars in Europe as the region’s policymakers try to curtail their exports. European Union officials said a deal with Beijing on Friday could halve the number of Chinese hybrid cars sent to the bloc in the next four years, helping to alleviate pressure on the European car industry. Officials are also discussing proposed rules that would prioritize European companies when public money is at stake. 中国公司正寻求在欧洲生产更多汽车，而欧洲政策制定者试图限制中国公司的出口。欧盟官员表示，周五与北京达成的一项协议可能使中国在未来四年向欧盟出口的混合动力汽车数量减半，有助于缓解欧洲汽车工业的压力。官员们还在讨论一项拟议规则，在涉及公共资金时优先考虑欧洲公司。 France’s president, Emmanuel Macron, who visited the event on Monday, has said Europe’s industries face a “life or death” moment. 法国总统马克龙周一参观了展会，他曾表示欧洲工业正面临“生死攸关”的时刻。 巴黎车展上的零跑B03。 Still, efforts to stem the flow could be just “a temporary respite, as in the medium term we see Chinese manufacturers near-shoring more to the E.U.,” said Matthias Schmidt, an analyst in Germany. Although companies such as Renault are keen to demonstrate their prowess, one prominent European company — BMW — opted not to attend. 中国的崛起是巴黎车展的新篇章。该车展于1898年首次在杜乐丽花园举办。此次尽管雷诺等公司急于展示其实力，但一家知名的欧洲公司——宝马——此次却选择缺席。 Chinese companies “have a big foot in the door,” said Serge Gachot, the director of the event and a former executive at Toyota and other companies. “They are very disruptive and fast moving.” 车展总监、曾任丰田等公司高管的塞尔日·加肖说，中国公司“已经一只脚牢牢踏进门内”。“它们极具颠覆性，而且行动迅速。” BYD’s sales in Europe have more than doubled this year, while sales of Chery and Leapmotor have grown at an even faster clip. After selling 700,000 cars back home, Xiaomi sees Germany as the foundation of its European expansion plans. 比亚迪今年在欧洲的销量增长了一倍多，奇瑞和零跑的销量增长更快。在中国本土售出70万辆汽车后，小米将德国视为其欧洲扩张计划的基础。 Chinese cars already account for about one in every 10 cars sold in Europe. And by teaming up with Chinese companies to keep their factories running, European manufacturers could end up helping their rivals. Yet they may have little choice but to cooperate and learn from their Chinese counterparts, said Ferdinand Dudenhöffer, an analyst and former industry executive. 中国汽车目前已占欧洲汽车销量的约十分之一。而欧洲制造商若为了维持工厂运转而与中国企业合作，最终可能会助长竞争对手的势头。但分析师、前行业高管费迪南德·杜登赫费尔说，它们可能别无选择，只能合作，并向中国同行学习。 “You can’t stand alone,” he said. “你不能单打独斗，”他说。 One of Zeekr’s mottos, “the power of a giant and a European soul,” is emblazoned on the wall of its exhibit. Sitting in the back of one of the Geely brand’s electric cars, its director in France, Rémy Aybaly, said he did not expect trade hurdles to hamper Zeekr’s ambitions. 极氪的口号之一“巨人的力量与欧洲的灵魂”醒目地展示在其展台墙上。坐在吉利品牌一款电动汽车的后座，该公司法国总监雷米·艾巴利表示，他不认为贸易障碍会阻碍极氪的雄心。 As for the Chinese companies, “you can see it as a threat, or you can see it as a chance” for Europe, he said. 他说，至于中国公司，“你可以将其视为威胁，也可以将其视为欧洲的机遇。” James Paton是时报国际商业和经济记者，常驻伦敦。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 揭秘俄罗斯鼠疫研究所：系统庞大隐秘，安全防护存疑
description: K. R. CALLAWAY2026年10月16日伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所发布的一张照片，显示2019年专家们在俄罗斯克拉斯诺亚尔斯克的一间实验室里工作。 Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Nearly two weeks after a 28-year-old researcher died from a mysterious infection while working in a Russian plague research laboratory, health officials around the world are still waiting for answers. 近两周前，一名在俄罗斯鼠疫研究实验室工作的28岁研究员因不明感染死亡，世界各地的卫生官员至今仍在等待答案。 Darya Shipilova, a lab worker at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute, was initially reported to have contracted pneumonic plague, raising concerns about the kinds of research being conducted at the facility and the safety measures employed there. 达里娅·希皮洛娃是伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所的一名实验室工作人员。最初有报道称她感染了肺鼠疫，这引发了人们对这家机构正在进行的研究种类及其安全措施的担忧。 The Russian authorities have since ruled out pneumonic plague, a bacterial infection caused by the same pathogen as the better known bubonic plague, as the cause of Ms. Shipilova’s death, but have yet to confirm which pathogen was responsible for causing her pneumonia. 此后，俄罗斯当局排除了肺鼠疫是希皮洛娃死因的可能性，但尚未确认导致她患上肺炎的病原体是什么。肺鼠疫是一种细菌感染，由与更为人熟知的腺鼠疫相同的病原体引起。 The incident, which led to denunciations by the United States and other governments, has exposed the international community’s lingering mistrust of Russian biomedical research, which harks back to the Soviet military’s once-robust programs for developing biological weapons. 这起事件引发美国及他国政府的谴责，也暴露出国际社会对俄罗斯生物医学研究挥之不去的怀疑。这种不信任可以追溯到苏联军方当年强大的生物武器研发计划。 The institute in Irkutsk never functioned as a military facility, but it was part of the broad yet secretive “Anti-Plague System.” At hundreds of field sites and labs across the Soviet Union, thousands of researchers were responsible for tracking emerging strains of plague and other endemic diseases, exterminating disease-causing rodents and developing vaccines. These facilities, experts said, had also provided pathogen samples to the military labs responsible for creating bioweapons during the Soviet era. 伊尔库茨克的这家研究所从未作为军事设施运作，但它是庞大而隐秘的“抗鼠疫系统”的一部分。在苏联各地的数百个野外站点和实验室中，数千名研究人员负责追踪新出现的鼠疫菌株和其他地方病，消灭致病啮齿动物并研发疫苗。专家表示，在苏联时代，这些机构还曾向负责研发生物武器的军事实验室提供病原体样本。 Most of these facilities are still functioning, and while those in Russia remain closely-guarded, some in former Soviet states have opened their doors to international researchers looking to learn about the fabled system. 这些机构大多数至今仍在运作。虽然俄罗斯境内的那些机构依然戒备森严，但一些位于前苏联加盟共和国的机构已经向国际研究人员敞开大门，让他们得以了解这个颇具传奇色彩的体系。 The Anti-Plague System 抗鼠疫系统 一张经过着色处理的鼠疫耶尔森菌扫描电子显微镜图像。这种细菌是鼠疫的病原体。 Although the Black Death of 14th-century Europe is the deadliest and best-known outbreak of the plague, a disease caused by the bacterium Y. pestis and carried by rodents, the illness has haunted Eurasia for thousands of years. 14世纪欧洲的黑死病是历史上死亡人数最多、也最为人熟知的一次鼠疫大流行，但这种由鼠疫耶尔森菌引起、通过啮齿动物传播的疾病已经困扰欧亚大陆数千年。 To put a stop to the frequent outbreaks in rural areas, where plague-harboring animals like rats, gerbils and marmots are endemic, the Soviet Union established a series of field sites and research institutes early in the 20th-century. They called it the “Anti-Plague System.” 为了遏制农村地区频繁暴发的疫情——那里广泛分布着携带鼠疫病原体的老鼠、沙鼠和旱獭等动物，苏联在20世纪初建立了一系列野外站点和研究机构，称之为“抗鼠疫系统”。 “The goal of their work was to be a central institute that surveils the vast areas around them, including the steppes that have large populations of burrowing wild rodents,” said Susan D. Jones, a veterinary historian at the University of Minnesota who in 2018 visited a former Soviet Anti-Plague Institute in what is now Kazakhstan. 明尼苏达大学研究兽医学历史的苏珊·琼斯说：“他们的目标是建立一个中心研究所，对周边广阔地区进行监测，包括穴居野生啮齿动物大量栖息的草原。”2018年，她曾参观了位于如今哈萨克斯坦境内的一家前苏联抗鼠疫研究所。 In its early days, the program was rudimentary. Scientists would venture on horseback into plague hot spots, often staying in tents or renting rooms from local residents, and would spend their days exterminating rodents, digging up their burrows and burning their food supplies in an attempt to eradicate the diseases they carried. 在早期，这项计划相当简陋。科学家骑马前往鼠疫高发地区，经常住在帐篷里，或向当地居民租房。他们每天捕杀啮齿动物，挖开这些动物的洞穴，焚烧它们的食物来源，试图消灭这些动物携带的疾病。 Many of these expeditions were conducted without effective disinfectants or personal protective equipment, making the job of Anti-Plague workers a very dangerous one. And the eradication efforts didn’t stop the spread of the disease. 许多此类考察是在没有有效消毒剂或个人防护装备的情况下进行的，这使得抗鼠疫工作人员的工作非常危险。而且灭鼠行动并未能阻止疾病传播。 Between the 1920s and 1950s, however, the program shifted its focus from eradication to outbreak prevention, opening up a series of labs in cities around the U.S.S.R. By the middle of the 20th century, as an antibiotic to treat plague was developed, thousands of year-round employees staffed these labs, with hundreds more hired seasonally to collect samples in the field. 不过，从20世纪20年代到50年代，该计划逐渐将重点从消灭鼠疫转向预防疫情暴发，并在苏联各地的城市建立了一系列实验室。到20世纪中叶，随着治疗鼠疫的抗生素问世，这些实验室已经雇用了数千名全年工作的员工，每年还会季节性雇用数百人到野外采集样本。 Inside the Soviet-Era Labs 苏联时代的实验室内部 2025年5月，西伯利亚和远东伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所的卫星照片。 The research conducted at these Soviet-era facilities was “hidden behind a curtain of secrecy,” a former anti-plague researcher, Dr. Moisey Iosifovich Levi, wrote in a 1994 essay. 前鼠疫防治研究员莫伊谢伊·约瑟福维奇·列维博士在1994年的一篇文章中写道，这些苏联时代的机构开展的研究“隐藏在保密的帷幕之后”。 To avoid links being made between their work and the bioweapon development programs in military labs, workers at the plague labs were instructed never to mention anything specific about their work in their conversations. 为了避免外界将他们的工作与军事实验室的生物武器研发计划联系起来，鼠疫实验室的工作人员接到指示，不得向他人透露工作细节。 Furthermore, the lab buildings themselves were built to look like normal housing units. Workers in many facilities maintained gardens, kept the lab windows open and walked around in normal clothing or even pajamas rather than wear white coats. 此外，实验室建筑本身也被设计成普通住宅的模样。许多机构的工作人员种植花草蔬菜，敞开实验室的窗户，穿着日常服装甚至睡衣走来走去，而不是穿白大褂。 It wasn’t until one stepped inside the lab and saw scientific equipment — refrigerators full of pathogen samples, large sterilizers boiling used equipment and long tables dotted with microscopes — that the buildings’ true purpose became apparent. 只有走进实验室，看到里面的科研设备——装满病原体样本的冰箱、对使用过的器械进行煮沸消毒的大型灭菌设备，以及摆满显微镜的长桌——人们才会发现这些建筑的真正用途。 Because of these unusual working conditions, “biosafety and biosecurity was very different from what we have in Western countries,” said Sonia Ben Ouagrham-Gormley, a biodefense researcher at George Mason University who has visited many anti-plague research institutes in former Soviet states. 乔治梅森大学的生物防御研究员索尼娅·本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利曾参观过前苏联国家的多家抗鼠疫研究所。她说，由于这些不寻常的工作条件，“那里的生物安全和生物安保措施与我们西方国家的做法大不相同”。 In a series of anthologies entitled “Interesting Stories of the Events and People of the Anti-Plague System of Russia and the Soviet Union,” edited by Dr. Levi, authors describe dangerous conditions that included outbreaks among animals kept in the facilities, lab fires and lost pathogen samples. 在列维博士主编的一套名为《俄罗斯和苏联抗鼠疫体系人物与事件趣闻》的文集中，作者们描述了种种危险状况，包括研究机构饲养的动物暴发疫情、实验室发生火灾，以及病原体样本丢失。 In the final years of the Soviet Union, several facilities were provided with safer and more effective lab equipment. Household refrigerators were swapped for more secure versions and fume hoods replaced open windows. But funding for these changes was difficult to come by, so smaller and more remote facilities, including the institute in Irkutsk, struggled to keep up. 苏联解体前的最后几年，一些机构获得了更安全、更有效的实验室设备。家用冰箱被替换成安全性更高的型号，通风橱取代了敞开的窗户。但这些改造所需的资金难以筹措，因此规模较小、地处偏远的机构难以跟上改进的步伐，伊尔库茨克研究所也是这类机构之一。 “In recent decades, much has changed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, and not for the better. In contrast with other Anti-Plague institutes, it did not get attention,” wrote a former director of the institute, Igor Valerianovich Domaradsky, in an essay included in Dr. Levi’s anthologies. 伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所前所长伊戈尔·瓦列里安诺维奇·多马拉茨基在收录于列维博士文集的一篇文章中写道：“近几十年来，伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所发生了很大变化，而且不是朝着好的方向。与其他抗鼠疫研究所相比，它没有得到关注。” “Therefore, the institute greatly lagged in acquiring new equipment and technology, which could not but affect the development of the institute,” he added. “What a shame.” 他接着写道：“因此，该研究所在获取新设备和新技术方面大大落后，这不可避免地影响了研究所的发展。真是令人遗憾。” The Facilities Today 这些机构的现状 俄罗斯伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究中心外，摄于10月7日。 After the fall of the Soviet Union, most labs, from the advanced centers in wealthy cities to financially struggling rural facilities, remained open. And for decades, many were largely unchanged. 苏联解体后，从富裕城市里的先进研究中心到资金拮据的农村机构，大多数实验室都继续运作。而且许多实验室在此后几十年里基本没有变化。 Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley visited over 100 former-Soviet facilities in the early 2000s, alongside colleagues from the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies. They found that entering one was like stepping into the past; tracking pathogen samples was done with pen and paper, and many vials were stored in oft-opened refrigerators, with wax seals used to indicate who had last opened them. 21世纪前几年，本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士与詹姆斯·马丁防扩散研究中心的同事一起，走访了100多处前苏联设施。他们发现，走进这些地方就仿佛回到了过去：病原体样本的追踪仍靠纸笔记录，许多样本瓶存放在经常打开的冰箱里，用蜡封表明谁最后打开过它们。 Many of the buildings, the researchers said, had no external security measures. And security inside was minimal, as well. 研究人员表示，许多建筑没有外部安保措施，内部的安全防护也非常有限。 “We got there for a visit, and in the lab there was a table under a window that was wide open, because it was a summer, and there’s no air conditioning, and there were piles of plague cultures on the table,” Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley said of one facility. 本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士在谈到其中一家机构时说：“我们去参观的时候，发现实验室里有一张桌子，就摆在一扇大开的窗户下面。因为是夏天，又没有空调，桌子上堆着一大堆鼠疫培养物。” Over the next two decades, several facilities in former Soviet states were refurbished or rebuilt to accommodate updated scientific equipment, allowing some to become state-of-the-art centers visited by researchers from around the world. 此后20年里，前苏联国家的一些机构得到翻修或重建，配备了更新的科研设备，其中一些因此成为最先进的研究中心，吸引世界各地的研究人员前来参观。 “There are levels of containment within these buildings,” Dr. Jones said of the facility that she visited in Kazakhstan in 2018. “Once one is in the most high level of containment, one will be wearing full P.P.E. and all work is done in sealed containment facilities.” 琼斯博士谈到她2018年参观的哈萨克斯坦一家研究机构时说：“这些建筑内部设有不同级别的生物防护区域。进入最高防护级别的区域后，工作人员必须穿戴全套个人防护装备，所有工作都在密闭的防护设施内进行。” Because Russia has kept its Anti-Plague System facilities closed to international researchers and government officials, it’s difficult to say for certain whether facilities in that country have improved as much as those that benefited from international aid to other states after the breakup of the Soviet Union. 由于俄罗斯一直不允许国际研究人员和他国政府官员进入其抗鼠疫体系的机构，很难确定俄罗斯境内设施的改进程度是否赶上了苏联解体后接受国际援助的其他前苏国家。 “I would assume that they have not improved much,” Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley said. “But they probably had maintained their procedures of Soviet time and their methods, which were good to ensure biosafety and prevent accidents in spite of a lack of equipment.” 本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士说：“我猜它们没有得到太大改善。但它们很可能保留了苏联时代的操作规程和方法。尽管缺乏设备，这些规程和方法在确保生物安全、防止事故方面还是相当有效的。” About the facility in Irkutsk, little information is publicly available. However, Russian authorities have remained adamant that Ms. Shipilova’s death was not the result of unfollowed protocols or lapses in biosecurity at the facility. 关于伊尔库茨克的这家研究所，公开信息很少。不过，俄罗斯当局始终坚称，希皮洛娃之死并非该机构未遵守操作规程或生物安保存在漏洞所致。 K. R. Callaway是时报科学记者，也是2026-2027时报Fellowship项目的成员，这是一个面向处于职业生涯初期的记者的培训项目。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site
