By the middle of the 20th century, as an antibiotic to treat plague was developed, thousands of year-round employees staffed these labs, with hundreds more hired seasonally to collect samples in the field. 不过，从20世纪20年代到50年代，该计划逐渐将重点从消灭鼠疫转向预防疫情暴发，并在苏联各地的城市建立了一系列实验室。到20世纪中叶，随着治疗鼠疫的抗生素问世，这些实验室已经雇用了数千名全年工作的员工，每年还会季节性雇用数百人到野外采集样本。 Inside the Soviet-Era Labs 苏联时代的实验室内部 2025年5月，西伯利亚和远东伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所的卫星照片。 The research conducted at these Soviet-era facilities was “hidden behind a curtain of secrecy,” a former anti-plague researcher, Dr. Moisey Iosifovich Levi, wrote in a 1994 essay. 前鼠疫防治研究员莫伊谢伊·约瑟福维奇·列维博士在1994年的一篇文章中写道，这些苏联时代的机构开展的研究“隐藏在保密的帷幕之后”。 To avoid links being made between their work and the bioweapon development programs in military labs, workers at the plague labs were instructed never to mention anything specific about their work in their conversations. 为了避免外界将他们的工作与军事实验室的生物武器研发计划联系起来，鼠疫实验室的工作人员接到指示，不得向他人透露工作细节。 Furthermore, the lab buildings themselves were built to look like normal housing units. Workers in many facilities maintained gardens, kept the lab windows open and walked around in normal clothing or even pajamas rather than wear white coats. 此外，实验室建筑本身也被设计成普通住宅的模样。许多机构的工作人员种植花草蔬菜，敞开实验室的窗户，穿着日常服装甚至睡衣走来走去，而不是穿白大褂。 It wasn’t until one stepped inside the lab and saw scientific equipment — refrigerators full of pathogen samples, large sterilizers boiling used equipment and long tables dotted with microscopes — that the buildings’ true purpose became apparent. 只有走进实验室，看到里面的科研设备——装满病原体样本的冰箱、对使用过的器械进行煮沸消毒的大型灭菌设备，以及摆满显微镜的长桌——人们才会发现这些建筑的真正用途。 Because of these unusual working conditions, “biosafety and biosecurity was very different from what we have in Western countries,” said Sonia Ben Ouagrham-Gormley, a biodefense researcher at George Mason University who has visited many anti-plague research institutes in former Soviet states. 乔治梅森大学的生物防御研究员索尼娅·本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利曾参观过前苏联国家的多家抗鼠疫研究所。她说，由于这些不寻常的工作条件，“那里的生物安全和生物安保措施与我们西方国家的做法大不相同”。 In a series of anthologies entitled “Interesting Stories of the Events and People of the Anti-Plague System of Russia and the Soviet Union,” edited by Dr. Levi, authors describe dangerous conditions that included outbreaks among animals kept in the facilities, lab fires and lost pathogen samples. 在列维博士主编的一套名为《俄罗斯和苏联抗鼠疫体系人物与事件趣闻》的文集中，作者们描述了种种危险状况，包括研究机构饲养的动物暴发疫情、实验室发生火灾，以及病原体样本丢失。 In the final years of the Soviet Union, several facilities were provided with safer and more effective lab equipment. Household refrigerators were swapped for more secure versions and fume hoods replaced open windows. But funding for these changes was difficult to come by, so smaller and more remote facilities, including the institute in Irkutsk, struggled to keep up. 苏联解体前的最后几年，一些机构获得了更安全、更有效的实验室设备。家用冰箱被替换成安全性更高的型号，通风橱取代了敞开的窗户。但这些改造所需的资金难以筹措，因此规模较小、地处偏远的机构难以跟上改进的步伐，伊尔库茨克研究所也是这类机构之一。 “In recent decades, much has changed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, and not for the better. In contrast with other Anti-Plague institutes, it did not get attention,” wrote a former director of the institute, Igor Valerianovich Domaradsky, in an essay included in Dr. Levi’s anthologies. 伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所前所长伊戈尔·瓦列里安诺维奇·多马拉茨基在收录于列维博士文集的一篇文章中写道：“近几十年来，伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究所发生了很大变化，而且不是朝着好的方向。与其他抗鼠疫研究所相比，它没有得到关注。” “Therefore, the institute greatly lagged in acquiring new equipment and technology, which could not but affect the development of the institute,” he added. “What a shame.” 他接着写道：“因此，该研究所在获取新设备和新技术方面大大落后，这不可避免地影响了研究所的发展。真是令人遗憾。” The Facilities Today 这些机构的现状 俄罗斯伊尔库茨克抗鼠疫研究中心外，摄于10月7日。 After the fall of the Soviet Union, most labs, from the advanced centers in wealthy cities to financially struggling rural facilities, remained open. And for decades, many were largely unchanged. 苏联解体后，从富裕城市里的先进研究中心到资金拮据的农村机构，大多数实验室都继续运作。而且许多实验室在此后几十年里基本没有变化。 Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley visited over 100 former-Soviet facilities in the early 2000s, alongside colleagues from the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies. They found that entering one was like stepping into the past; tracking pathogen samples was done with pen and paper, and many vials were stored in oft-opened refrigerators, with wax seals used to indicate who had last opened them. 21世纪前几年，本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士与詹姆斯·马丁防扩散研究中心的同事一起，走访了100多处前苏联设施。他们发现，走进这些地方就仿佛回到了过去：病原体样本的追踪仍靠纸笔记录，许多样本瓶存放在经常打开的冰箱里，用蜡封表明谁最后打开过它们。 Many of the buildings, the researchers said, had no external security measures. And security inside was minimal, as well. 研究人员表示，许多建筑没有外部安保措施，内部的安全防护也非常有限。 “We got there for a visit, and in the lab there was a table under a window that was wide open, because it was a summer, and there’s no air conditioning, and there were piles of plague cultures on the table,” Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley said of one facility. 本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士在谈到其中一家机构时说：“我们去参观的时候，发现实验室里有一张桌子，就摆在一扇大开的窗户下面。因为是夏天，又没有空调，桌子上堆着一大堆鼠疫培养物。” Over the next two decades, several facilities in former Soviet states were refurbished or rebuilt to accommodate updated scientific equipment, allowing some to become state-of-the-art centers visited by researchers from around the world. 此后20年里，前苏联国家的一些机构得到翻修或重建，配备了更新的科研设备，其中一些因此成为最先进的研究中心，吸引世界各地的研究人员前来参观。 “There are levels of containment within these buildings,” Dr. Jones said of the facility that she visited in Kazakhstan in 2018. “Once one is in the most high level of containment, one will be wearing full P.P.E. and all work is done in sealed containment facilities.” 琼斯博士谈到她2018年参观的哈萨克斯坦一家研究机构时说：“这些建筑内部设有不同级别的生物防护区域。进入最高防护级别的区域后，工作人员必须穿戴全套个人防护装备，所有工作都在密闭的防护设施内进行。” Because Russia has kept its Anti-Plague System facilities closed to international researchers and government officials, it’s difficult to say for certain whether facilities in that country have improved as much as those that benefited from international aid to other states after the breakup of the Soviet Union. 由于俄罗斯一直不允许国际研究人员和他国政府官员进入其抗鼠疫体系的机构，很难确定俄罗斯境内设施的改进程度是否赶上了苏联解体后接受国际援助的其他前苏国家。 “I would assume that they have not improved much,” Dr. Ben Ouagrham-Gormley said. “But they probably had maintained their procedures of Soviet time and their methods, which were good to ensure biosafety and prevent accidents in spite of a lack of equipment.” 本·瓦格拉姆-戈姆利博士说：“我猜它们没有得到太大改善。但它们很可能保留了苏联时代的操作规程和方法。尽管缺乏设备，这些规程和方法在确保生物安全、防止事故方面还是相当有效的。” About the facility in Irkutsk, little information is publicly available. However, Russian authorities have remained adamant that Ms. Shipilova’s death was not the result of unfollowed protocols or lapses in biosecurity at the facility. 关于伊尔库茨克的这家研究所，公开信息很少。不过，俄罗斯当局始终坚称，希皮洛娃之死并非该机构未遵守操作规程或生物安保存在漏洞所致。 K. R. Callaway 是时报科学记者，也是2026-2027时报 Fellowship 项目的成员，这是一个面向处于职业生涯初期的记者的培训项目。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

title: 新鸭绿江大桥通车，中朝贸易关系升温
description: CHOE SANG-HUN2026年10月16日周四，从中国丹东眺望正式开通的新鸭绿江大桥。 Iori Sagisawa/Kyodo News, via Associated Press North Korea and China on Thursday opened the New Yalu River Bridge, the largest border crossing between the two countries, a sign of growing trade despite international sanctions aimed at constraining North Korea’s economy and nuclear weapons program. 周四，朝鲜与中国开通了两国间最大的边境通道——新鸭绿江大桥。尽管旨在遏制朝鲜经济及核武器计划的国际制裁依然存在，此举表明双边贸易正在不断增长。 In recent weeks, travelers returning from the river border reported that trucks and cars were already crossing the four-lane, nearly two-mile long bridge from China into North Korea. The bridge connects the Chinese city of Dandong to Sinuiju, a North Korean city on the Yalu River that forms much of the border between the two countries. 最近几周，从边境江段返回的旅客反映，已有卡车和客车经由这座双向四车道、长约三公里的大桥从中国驶入朝鲜。这座桥梁连接中国丹东市与坐落于鸭绿江畔的朝鲜城市新义州，鸭绿江构成了两国间的大部分边界。 Its opening, which was reported by the Chinese state media, comes just a month after North Korea and Russia inaugurated their first — and much smaller — road bridge across the Tumen River border. The consecutive bridge openings underscore Pyongyang’s deepening ties with its two main allies. 据中国官方媒体报道，这座桥梁通车距朝俄启用横跨图们江边境、规模小得多的首座公路桥仅相隔一个月。两座跨境桥梁的相继启用凸显出平壤正在深化与这两大主要盟友的关系。 In a video address at the opening ceremony, Premier Li Qiang of China said the new bridge “will not only strongly promote bilateral economic and trade cooperation but also further strengthen people-to-people exchanges,” according to Chinese state media. Prime Minister Pak Thae-song of North Korea also delivered a speech via video, it said. 据中国官方媒体报道，中国国务院总理李强在开通仪式上发表视频致辞时表示，新大桥“不仅将有力促进两国经贸合作，也将进一步密切双方人员往来”。报道称，朝鲜内阁总理朴泰成亦通过视频致辞。 Russia built its road bridge to supplement its lone rail link with North Korea after Pyongyang sent weapons and troops to aid Moscow’s war against Ukraine. As North Korea’s relationship with Russia has strengthened, China has moved to expand its own trade with Pyongyang in an effort to maintain its economic influence over its neighbor. 随着平壤向对乌克兰作战的莫斯科提供武器和军事人员援助，俄罗斯建造了公路桥，以弥补其与朝鲜间单一铁路连接的不足。随着朝俄关系不断强化，中国也着手扩大对朝贸易，力求保持对该邻国的经济影响力。 Moscow and Beijing had already weakened the international sanctions against North Korea when they worked together in 2024 to dissolve the United Nations panel responsible for monitoring the enforcement of sanctions. Both countries have also urged Washington to ease restrictions on Pyongyang, arguing that the sanctions have failed to halt the country’s nuclear weapons development. 早在2024年，莫斯科与北京联手解散了负责监督制裁执行情况的联合国专家小组，从而削弱了针对朝鲜的国际制裁。两国还敦促华盛顿放宽对朝限制，主张制裁并未能阻止朝鲜研发核武器。 Analysts warn that these new bridges could serve as a trade route for North Korea, whose economy has been strained by U.N. sanctions that prohibit key exports, including coal and labor, and severely restrict fuel imports. 分析人士警告称，这些新建桥梁可能成为朝鲜的贸易通道。受制于联合国禁止煤炭和劳工等关键出口并严控燃料进口的制裁措施，朝鲜经济此前已承受重压。 Until now, Sinuiju and Dandong were linked primarily by the 83-year-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which features just a single rail line and one road lane. The aging structure could not hold trucks weighing over 20 tons and had a strict three-mile-per-hour speed limit. In 2009, China proposed building the wider New Yalu River Bridge as part of broader efforts to bring North Korea further into its economic sphere. 此前，新义州与丹东主要依靠拥有83年历史的中朝友谊桥相连，该桥仅设一条单轨铁路和一条公路。这座老化的桥梁无法承载20吨以上的货车，且需严格保持每小时约4.8公里的限速。2009年，中国提议建造桥面更宽的新鸭绿江大桥，作为将朝鲜进一步纳入自身经济辐射范围的更广泛举措之一。 Construction was completed in 2014, with China footing the bill estimated at $329 million. But the opening was delayed for 12 years, as North Korea took time building connecting roads, customs stations and supporting facilities. 该工程于2014年竣工，耗资约3.29亿美元且全额由中方承担。但因朝方耗时修建连接道路、海关检查站及配套设施，通车时间被推迟了12年。 But Pyongyang was also concerned about becoming even more dependent on China. Decades of international sanctions have left North Korea reliant on China for nearly all of its external trade. After the U.N. Security Council blacklisted North Korea’s top exports, the country’s trade deficit with China ballooned. 平壤方面也担忧对华依赖进一步加深。数十年的国际制裁使朝鲜在几乎所有对外贸易上均依赖中国；在联合国安理会将朝鲜主要出口产品列入黑名单后，该国对华贸易逆差急剧攀升。 “From North Korea’s perspective, the opening of the New Yalu River Bridge could allow Chinese goods to enter more quickly and in larger volumes, with no guarantee that North Korea could significantly increase its own exports to China,” said Kim Gyu-beom, an analyst at the Seoul-based Institute for National Security Strategy. “There is little incentive for North Korea to welcome a scenario in which its trade deficit and dependence on China continue to deepen.” 位于首尔的国家安保战略研究院分析师金奎范（音）表示：“从朝鲜的角度来看，新鸭绿江大桥的开通可能促使中国商品更快捷、更大规模地进入，却无法确保朝鲜能大幅增加对华出口。”他指出：“若贸易逆差与对华依赖持续加深，这没有理由成为朝鲜所乐见的前景。” Analysts suggested that before agreeing to open the bridge, North Korea may have sought concessions that would facilitate exports to China and create opportunities for more North Korean workers to be employed there. 分析人士指出，在同意大桥通车前，朝鲜可能争取过某些优惠条件，以便利本国对华出口，并为更多朝鲜劳工在华务工创造机会。 North Korea’s leader, Kim Jong-un, has faced the challenge of importing the Chinese raw materials and equipment needed to rebuild his economy while also raising hard currency. North Korea has largely accomplished the latter through illicit means such as smuggling, sending workers overseas, cyber operations and cryptocurrency theft. 朝鲜领导人金正恩面临着双重挑战，既要进口重建其经济所需的中国原材料和设备，又需筹集硬通货。朝鲜主要通过走私、向海外输出劳工、网络行动以及盗窃加密货币等非法手段来实现了外汇目标。 Mr. Kim pushed his country to produce more consumer goods domestically while cracking down on the smuggling of such products from China, using the Covid-19 pandemic as justification. He has also sought to reduce the chronic trade imbalance by attracting Chinese tourists to newly built coastal and mountain resorts across North Korea. 金正恩以新冠疫情为由严打自华走私消费品，同时要求国内增产此类产品。他还试图通过吸引中国游客前往朝鲜各地新建的沿海与山区度假胜地，来缓解长期的贸易失衡状况。 China accelerated its re-engagement with North Korea after Pyongyang grew closer to Moscow during the Ukraine war. China’s leader, Xi Jinping, invited both Mr. Kim and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia to a military parade in Beijing last year. Rail service between Beijing and Pyongyang, suspended during the pandemic, resumed in March, and Mr. Xi visited Pyongyang in June. 随着平壤在乌克兰战争期间向莫斯科靠拢，中国加快了与朝鲜重新接触的步伐。去年，中国领导人习近平邀请金正恩与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京出席北京的阅兵式。疫情期间暂停的京平客运列车已于3月恢复运行，习近平6月访问了平壤。 Official trade between North Korea and China reached $1.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese data, hitting its highest level since comprehensive U.N. sanctions were fully implemented in 2017. 中国官方数据显示，今年上半年朝中官方贸易额达15亿美元，创下2017年联合国全面制裁完全落地以来的最高水平。 Choe Sang-Hun是时报驻首尔首席记者，报道韩国和朝鲜新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

Prime Minister Pak Thae-song of North Korea also delivered a speech via video, it said. 据中国官方媒体报道 ，中国国务院总理李强在开通仪式上发表视频致辞时表示，新大桥“不仅将有力促进两国经贸合作，也将进一步密切双方人员往来”。报道称，朝鲜内阁总理朴泰成亦通过视频致辞。 Russia built its road bridge to supplement its lone rail link with North Korea after Pyongyang sent weapons and troops to aid Moscow’s war against Ukraine. As North Korea’s relationship with Russia has strengthened, China has moved to expand its own trade with Pyongyang in an effort to maintain its economic influence over its neighbor. 随着平壤向对乌克兰作战的莫斯科提供武器和军事人员援助，俄罗斯建造了公路桥，以弥补其与朝鲜间单一铁路连接的不足。随着朝俄关系不断强化，中国也着手扩大对朝贸易，力求保持对该邻国的经济影响力。 Moscow and Beijing had already weakened the international sanctions against North Korea when they worked together in 2024 to dissolve the United Nations panel responsible for monitoring the enforcement of sanctions. Both countries have also urged Washington to ease restrictions on Pyongyang, arguing that the sanctions have failed to halt the country’s nuclear weapons development. 早在2024年，莫斯科与北京联手解散了负责监督制裁执行情况的联合国专家小组，从而削弱了针对朝鲜的国际制裁。两国还敦促华盛顿放宽对朝限制，主张制裁并未能阻止朝鲜研发核武器。 Analysts warn that these new bridges could serve as a trade route for North Korea, whose economy has been strained by U.N. sanctions that prohibit key exports, including coal and labor, and severely restrict fuel imports. 分析人士警告称，这些新建桥梁可能成为朝鲜的贸易通道。受制于联合国禁止煤炭和劳工等关键出口并严控燃料进口的制裁措施，朝鲜经济此前已承受重压。 Until now, Sinuiju and Dandong were linked primarily by the 83-year-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which features just a single rail line and one road lane. The aging structure could not hold trucks weighing over 20 tons and had a strict three-mile-per-hour speed limit. In 2009, China proposed building the wider New Yalu River Bridge as part of broader efforts to bring North Korea further into its economic sphere. 此前，新义州与丹东主要依靠拥有83年历史的中朝友谊桥相连，该桥仅设一条单轨铁路和一条公路。这座老化的桥梁无法承载20吨以上的货车，且需严格保持每小时约4.8公里的限速。2009年，中国提议建造桥面更宽的新鸭绿江大桥，作为将朝鲜进一步纳入自身经济辐射范围的更广泛举措之一。 Construction was completed in 2014, with China footing the bill estimated at $329 million. But the opening was delayed for 12 years, as North Korea took time building connecting roads, customs stations and supporting facilities. 该工程于2014年竣工，耗资约3.29亿美元且全额由中方承担。但因朝方耗时修建连接道路、海关检查站及配套设施，通车时间被推迟了12年。 But Pyongyang was also concerned about becoming even more dependent on China. Decades of international sanctions have left North Korea reliant on China for nearly all of its external trade. After the U.N. Security Council blacklisted North Korea’s top exports, the country’s trade deficit with China ballooned. 平壤方面也担忧对华依赖进一步加深。数十年的国际制裁使朝鲜在几乎所有对外贸易上均依赖中国；在联合国安理会将朝鲜主要出口产品列入黑名单后，该国对华贸易逆差急剧攀升。 “From North Korea’s perspective, the opening of the New Yalu River Bridge could allow Chinese goods to enter more quickly and in larger volumes, with no guarantee that North Korea could significantly increase its own exports to China,” said Kim Gyu-beom , an analyst at the Seoul-based Institute for National Security Strategy. “There is little incentive for North Korea to welcome a scenario in which its trade deficit and dependence on China continue to deepen.” 位于首尔的国家安保战略研究院分析师 金奎范 （音）表示：“从朝鲜的角度来看，新鸭绿江大桥的开通可能促使中国商品更快捷、更大规模地进入，却无法确保朝鲜能大幅增加对华出口。”他指出：“若贸易逆差与对华依赖持续加深，这没有理由成为朝鲜所乐见的前景。” Analysts suggested that before agreeing to open the bridge, North Korea may have sought concessions that would facilitate exports to China and create opportunities for more North Korean workers to be employed there. 分析人士指出，在同意大桥通车前，朝鲜可能争取过某些优惠条件，以便利本国对华出口，并为更多朝鲜劳工在华务工创造机会。 North Korea’s leader, Kim Jong-un, has faced the challenge of importing the Chinese raw materials and equipment needed to rebuild his economy while also raising hard currency. North Korea has largely accomplished the latter through illicit means such as smuggling, sending workers overseas, cyber operations and cryptocurrency theft. 朝鲜领导人金正恩面临着双重挑战，既要进口重建其经济所需的中国原材料和设备，又需筹集硬通货。朝鲜主要通过走私、向海外输出劳工、 网络行动 以及盗窃加密货币等 非法手段 来实现了外汇目标。 Mr. Kim pushed his country to produce more consumer goods domestically while cracking down on the smuggling of such products from China, using the Covid-19 pandemic as justification . He has also sought to reduce the chronic trade imbalance by attracting Chinese tourists to newly built coastal and mountain resorts across North Korea. 金正恩 以新冠疫情为由 严打自华走私消费品，同时要求国内增产此类产品。他还试图通过吸引中国游客前往朝鲜各地新建的 沿海与山区度假胜地 ，来缓解长期的贸易失衡状况。 China accelerated its re-engagement with North Korea after Pyongyang grew closer to Moscow during the Ukraine war. China’s leader, Xi Jinping, invited both Mr. Kim and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia to a military parade in Beijing last year. Rail service between Beijing and Pyongyang, suspended during the pandemic, resumed in March, and Mr. Xi visited Pyongyang in June. 随着平壤在乌克兰战争期间向莫斯科靠拢，中国加快了与朝鲜重新接触的步伐。去年，中国领导人习近平 邀请 金正恩与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·V·普京出席北京的阅兵式。疫情期间暂停的京平客运列车已于3月恢复运行，习近平6月 访问了平壤 。 Official trade between North Korea and China reached $1.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese data, hitting its highest level since comprehensive U.N. sanctions were fully implemented in 2017. 中国官方数据显示，今年上半年朝中官方贸易额达15亿美元，创下2017年联合国全面制裁完全落地以来的最高水平。 Choe Sang-Hun 是时报驻首尔首席记者，报道韩国和朝鲜新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 星盾使用受限、俄方袭击升级：乌克兰“腹背受敌”
description: CONSTANT MÉHEUT2026年10月15日周三，基辅一栋公寓楼遭袭现场，消防员正在进行灭火作业。 Evgeniy Maloletka/Associated Press Nearly five years into its fight for national survival, Ukraine has entered a moment of intense vulnerability, under growing pressure not only from Russia but also now from the United States. 在为国家生存而战近五年之后，乌克兰陷入了一个异常脆弱的时刻，不仅来自俄罗斯的压力越来越大，如今美国也在施压。 A double blow came overnight on Wednesday. 周三夜间，乌克兰接连遭受两次打击。 Ukraine said that its military, with no warning, had lost some critical access to a military version of Starlink, a pillar of its battlefield communications. Kyiv relies on the satellite internet network, known as Starshield, which is paid for by the Pentagon. That led Ukrainian officials and analysts to surmise that the restrictions had come from Washington, as President Trump is locked in his latest feud with Ukraine’s leadership. 乌克兰表示，在没有收到任何预警的情况下，乌军突然失去了对军事版星链系统部分关键功能的使用权限，而这是乌克兰战场通信的重要支柱。基辅依赖这个名为星盾的卫星互联网网络，费用由五角大楼支付。乌克兰官员和分析人士因此推测，这些限制来自华盛顿，因为特朗普总统正与乌克兰领导层陷入新一轮争执。 At the same time, Russia unleashed dozens of ballistic missiles in a broad attack on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure early Wednesday, cutting power to 600,000 people in the capital, Kyiv. It was a dark omen for a rapidly approaching winter in which Russia is gearing up to try to push Ukraine to the breaking point as Kyiv runs low on lifesaving air defenses. 与此同时，俄罗斯周三凌晨发动大规模袭击，向乌克兰能源基础设施发射了数十枚弹道导弹，导致首都基辅60万人断电。随着冬季迅速临近，这无疑是一个不祥的预兆。俄罗斯正准备在冬季进一步施压，试图将乌克兰逼至崩溃边缘，而基辅用于救命的防空力量日益薄弱。 It was unclear how long the Starshield restrictions would remain in place. Still, the Trump administration’s treatment of Ukraine has caused outrage in a country already reeling from a string of challenges. 目前尚不清楚星盾的使用限制会持续多久。不过，特朗普政府对待乌克兰的方式已经在这个接连遭受重重打击的国家激起愤怒。 Its energy system is at risk of collapse in the coming months as Russia pounds power plants and substations, trying to deprive Ukrainians of heat and water. Its economy is being pushed to the brink by Russian strikes on its ports, warehouses and steel factories. And its budget faces a multibillion-dollar gap this year and next that could leave its military severely underfunded. 随着俄罗斯不断轰炸乌克兰的发电厂和变电站，企图切断乌克兰的供暖和供水，该国能源系统在未来几个月有崩溃的风险。俄罗斯对乌克兰港口、仓库和钢铁厂的袭击正将乌克兰经济推向崩溃边缘。与此同时，乌克兰今明两年的预算面临数十亿美元的缺口，可能导致军费严重不足。 The Starshield development was interpreted in Ukraine as part of a Trump administration pressure campaign to limit Ukraine’s ability to fight. Mr. Trump is pushing Kyiv to stop attacking oil refineries so that Russia can pump more diesel onto global markets as high prices threaten the prospects of Mr. Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections. 在乌克兰，星盾系统遭到限制一事被解读为特朗普政府施压行动的一部分，目的是削弱乌克兰的作战能力。特朗普正敦促基辅停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂，以便俄罗斯向全球市场供应更多柴油。目前，高油价正威胁特朗普所属共和党在中期选举中的前景。 “Clearly, this action cannot be a coincidence and is linked to the current political situation,” Serhiy Beskrestnov, a Ukrainian military expert who advises President Volodymyr Zelensky on weapons technologies, wrote on social media about the Starlink restrictions. “显然，这一行动不可能是巧合，而是与当前政治局势有关，”为泽连斯基总统提供武器技术咨询的乌克兰军事专家谢尔希·别斯克列斯特诺夫在社交媒体上评论星链限制措施时写道。 SpaceX, which operates Starlink and Starshield, and its chief executive, Elon Musk, did not respond to requests for comment. The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 运营星链和星盾的SpaceX及其首席执行官埃隆·马斯克均未回应置评请求。五角大楼也没有立即回应置评请求。 Ukraine was stunned to discover the Starshield restrictions, which it said caused disruptions to several combat operations. The Ukrainian military uses Starshield in part to guide its ever-growing fleets of drones, including interceptors used to down Russian drones. The restrictions, Ukrainian officials said, tied Ukraine’s hands while leaving Russia free to wage war. 乌克兰军方震惊地发现，星盾系统突然受到限制，并表示这干扰了多项作战行动。乌军使用星盾系统的一个重要用途是为规模不断扩大的无人机机队提供导航，包括用于击落俄罗斯无人机的拦截机。乌克兰官员表示，这些限制束缚了乌克兰的手脚，却让俄罗斯可以放手作战。 Perhaps nowhere was that imbalance clearer than in the Russian air assault overnight. The barrage included 39 ballistic missiles, Mr. Zelensky said. That would be the largest such salvo during the entire war, according to a New York Times data set based on Ukrainian Air Force figures. 这种不对等局面在俄罗斯夜间发动的空袭中表现得尤为明显。泽连斯基表示，这轮袭击包括39枚弹道导弹。根据《纽约时报》依据乌克兰空军数据建立的数据集，这是整场战争期间规模最大的一次弹道导弹齐射。 Even as Russia pounds Ukraine day after day, leading to some of the highest civilian death tolls seen in years of war, Kyiv says it is abiding by Mr. Trump’s demand not to strike Russian oil refineries. Its campaign against refineries, which had led to fuel shortages across Russia, made Russians feel the war as never before. 尽管俄罗斯日复一日地猛烈轰炸乌克兰，造成多年来最严重的平民伤亡，基辅表示，自己仍在遵守特朗普停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂的要求。此前，乌克兰针对炼油厂的袭击行动导致俄罗斯各地出现燃料短缺，让俄罗斯民众以前所未有的程度感受到战争的影响。 Kyiv has said it is unfair that Russia is still attacking Ukraine’s power plants and substations. Mr. Zelensky has asserted that the strikes violate Mr. Trump’s self-declared energy cease-fire in Ukraine. The Trump administration views the cease-fire as covering only strikes on oil refineries, even though Ukraine has none that are operational. 基辅表示，俄罗斯仍在袭击乌克兰的发电厂和变电站，这有失公平。泽连斯基坚称，这些袭击违反了特朗普自行宣布的乌克兰能源停火安排。特朗普政府则认为，这项停火安排仅涵盖针对炼油厂的袭击，尽管乌克兰目前并没有仍在运营的炼油厂。 救援人员正在转移一名在基辅公寓楼袭击中受伤的居民。 Ukraine has set aside its most potent tool against Russia in part because it is worried that Mr. Trump could follow through on an apparent threat to stop providing intelligence that Kyiv needs to warn its people of incoming Russian strikes. 乌克兰搁置了它对付俄罗斯最有力的手段，部分原因是担心特朗普可能兑现其停止提供情报的威胁。基辅需要这些情报，才能向民众预警俄罗斯即将发动的袭击。 While Ukraine’s European partners have so far stepped in to patch Ukraine’s ballooning budget gaps as Russia batters the Ukrainian economy, Europe is not believed to be able to fully fill intelligence deficits if the United States were to pull back. 在俄罗斯持续打击乌克兰经济之际，乌克兰的欧洲伙伴一直在帮助填补该国不断扩大的预算缺口。但外界普遍认为，如果美国撤出，欧洲将无法完全弥补由此产生的缺口。 Ukrainian fears have been elevated over the past two days as Mr. Zelensky has reported that Ukraine did not receive early warnings about Russian missile strikes, though Mr. Trump said on Tuesday that intelligence was still being shared. 过去两天，乌克兰的担忧进一步加剧。泽连斯基报告称，乌方没有收到俄罗斯导弹袭击的预警，尽管特朗普周二表示，美国仍在与乌克兰分享情报。 The Ukrainian Air Force clarified on Wednesday that while it had received no advance warning before a Russian missile struck at about 10:40 p.m. on Tuesday, it did receive warnings related to three subsequent waves of attacks that night. Such intelligence sharing is separate from Ukraine’s use of the Starshield system. 乌克兰空军周三澄清说，虽然周二晚间10时40分左右，一枚俄罗斯导弹来袭前，乌方没有收到提前预警，但对于当晚随后发生的三波袭击，乌方确实收到了预警。这类情报共享与乌克兰使用星盾系统是两回事。 The Starshield limitations, if they continue, could hobble Ukraine’s military operations. Starshield terminals are used for nearly everything the Ukrainian Army deploys on the battlefield: the cars that carry troops and matériel, the drones that ferry food and water to soldiers at the front, and the attack drones that fly long distances to hit Russian positions. 如果星盾的使用限制持续下去，乌克兰的军事行动可能受到严重阻碍。从运送部队和物资的车辆，到向前线士兵运送食物和饮水的无人机，再到远程飞行打击俄军阵地的攻击无人机，乌军投入战场的几乎所有装备都要用到星盾终端。 The Ukrainian military uses thousands of terminals connected to Starshield, a version of the Starlink network that is harder to hack or jam. Mr. Musk said earlier this year that Starshield was “operated by the U.S. government.” 乌克兰军方使用数以千计与星盾相连的终端。星盾是星链网络的一个版本，更难被黑客攻击或干扰。马斯克今年早些时候说过，星盾由“美国政府运营”。 2023年，乌克兰顿涅茨克地区东部前线附近，一台经过伪装的星链天线。乌克兰军方使用该系统，部分用于引导其不断壮大的无人机机群。 Sasha Maslov for The New York Times Officials from Ukraine’s defense ministry said on Wednesday that, without warning, SpaceX had restricted the use of Starshield for devices traveling faster than 100 miles per hour. When the device exceeded this speed, the terminals lost connection. The officials said the ministry was in touch with the U.S. government, SpaceX and NATO partners to address the issue. 乌克兰国防部官员周三表示，SpaceX在没有事先发出任何通知的情况下，限制了星盾在移动速度超过每小时100英里（约160公里）设备上的使用。一旦设备超过这一速度，终端就会断开连接。官员们说，国防部正在与美国政府、SpaceX和北约伙伴联系，以解决这个问题。 Ukrainian soldiers said missions had been disrupted as a result. Oleksandr, an officer in the 8th Air Assault Corps, said the restrictions had mainly affected heavy bomber and fixed-wing drones targeting Russian logistical routes and positions in occupied territory. He spoke on the condition that he be identified by only his first name, in keeping with Ukrainian military rules. 乌克兰士兵表示，相关限制已经干扰了作战任务。第八空中突击军军官亚历山大说，受影响的主要是重型轰炸无人机和固定翼无人机的作战行动。这些无人机用于打击俄罗斯在乌克兰占领区的后勤补给线和军事阵地。出于乌克兰军方规定，他只允许透露名字。 Oleksandr said that if the restrictions remained in effect, Russia would be able to reopen crucial supply routes in a matter of days, and could better protect expensive equipment, including ships, from Ukrainian attacks. 亚历山大表示，如果这些限制继续实施，俄罗斯将在几天内重新打通关键补给路线，并能更有效地保护包括舰船在内的昂贵装备，免遭乌克兰的袭击。 Starshield also provides connections to the interceptor drones that Ukraine uses to shoot down the Russian attack drones known as Shaheds, especially the fast-flying jet-powered models that Russia is now launching toward Ukraine en masse, said Mr. Beskrestnov, the military-technology adviser to Mr. Zelensky. 泽连斯基的军事技术顾问别斯克列斯特诺夫表示，星盾还为乌克兰用于击落俄罗斯“见证者”攻击无人机的拦截无人机提供通信连接，特别是在应对俄罗斯如今大规模发射、飞行速度极快的喷气动力型号时。 “In effect, our partners’ actions are depriving us of one of the few ways we have to defend the country against jet-powered Shaheds,” Mr. Beskrestnov said. “实际上，我们的伙伴正在通过这些行动剥夺我们保卫国家、抵御喷气动力‘见证者’无人机的为数不多的手段之一，”别斯克列斯特诺夫说。 Ryan Mac、Carlotta Gall、Siobhán O’Grady和Maria Varenikova对本文有报道贡献。 Constant Méheut是时报记者，报道乌克兰战争。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

Kyiv relies on the satellite internet network, known as Starshield, which is paid for by the Pentagon. That led Ukrainian officials and analysts to surmise that the restrictions had come from Washington, as President Trump is locked in his latest feud with Ukraine’s leadership. 乌克兰表示，在没有收到任何预警的情况下，乌军突然失去了对军事版星链系统部分关键功能的使用权限，而这是乌克兰战场通信的重要支柱。基辅依赖这个名为星盾的卫星互联网网络，费用由五角大楼支付。乌克兰官员和分析人士因此推测，这些限制来自华盛顿，因为特朗普总统正与乌克兰领导层 陷入新一轮争执 。 At the same time, Russia unleashed dozens of ballistic missiles in a broad attack on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure early Wednesday, cutting power to 600,000 people in the capital, Kyiv. It was a dark omen for a rapidly approaching winter in which Russia is gearing up to try to push Ukraine to the breaking point as Kyiv runs low on lifesaving air defenses. 与此同时，俄罗斯周三凌晨发动大规模袭击，向乌克兰能源基础设施发射了数十枚弹道导弹，导致首都基辅60万人断电。随着冬季迅速临近，这无疑是一个不祥的预兆。俄罗斯正准备在冬季进一步施压，试图将乌克兰逼至崩溃边缘，而基辅用于救命的防空力量日益薄弱。 It was unclear how long the Starshield restrictions would remain in place. Still, the Trump administration’s treatment of Ukraine has caused outrage in a country already reeling from a string of challenges. 目前尚不清楚星盾的使用限制会持续多久。不过，特朗普政府对待乌克兰的方式已经在这个接连遭受重重打击的国家激起愤怒。 Its energy system is at risk of collapse in the coming months as Russia pounds power plants and substations, trying to deprive Ukrainians of heat and water. Its economy is being pushed to the brink by Russian strikes on its ports, warehouses and steel factories. And its budget faces a multibillion-dollar gap this year and next that could leave its military severely underfunded. 随着俄罗斯不断轰炸乌克兰的发电厂和变电站，企图切断乌克兰的供暖和供水， 该国能源系统在未来几个月有崩溃的风险 。俄罗斯对乌克兰港口、仓库和钢铁厂的袭击正 将乌克兰经济推向崩溃边缘 。与此同时，乌克兰今明两年的预算面临数十亿美元的缺口，可能导致军费严重不足。 The Starshield development was interpreted in Ukraine as part of a Trump administration pressure campaign to limit Ukraine’s ability to fight. Mr. Trump is pushing Kyiv to stop attacking oil refineries so that Russia can pump more diesel onto global markets as high prices threaten the prospects of Mr. Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections. 在乌克兰，星盾系统遭到限制一事被解读为特朗普政府施压行动的一部分，目的是削弱乌克兰的作战能力。特朗普正敦促基辅停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂，以便俄罗斯向全球市场供应更多柴油。目前，高油价正威胁特朗普所属共和党在中期选举中的前景。 “Clearly, this action cannot be a coincidence and is linked to the current political situation,” Serhiy Beskrestnov, a Ukrainian military expert who advises President Volodymyr Zelensky on weapons technologies, wrote on social media about the Starlink restrictions. “显然，这一行动不可能是巧合，而是与当前政治局势有关，”为泽连斯基总统提供武器技术咨询的乌克兰军事专家谢尔希·别斯克列斯特诺夫在 社交媒体 上评论星链限制措施时写道。 SpaceX, which operates Starlink and Starshield, and its chief executive, Elon Musk, did not respond to requests for comment. The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 运营星链和星盾的SpaceX及其首席执行官埃隆·马斯克均未回应置评请求。五角大楼也没有立即回应置评请求。 Ukraine was stunned to discover the Starshield restrictions, which it said caused disruptions to several combat operations. The Ukrainian military uses Starshield in part to guide its ever-growing fleets of drones , including interceptors used to down Russian drones. The restrictions, Ukrainian officials said, tied Ukraine’s hands while leaving Russia free to wage war. 乌克兰军方震惊地发现，星盾系统突然受到限制，并表示这干扰了多项作战行动。乌军使用星盾系统的一个重要用途是为 规模不断扩大的无人机机队 提供导航，包括用于击落俄罗斯无人机的拦截机。乌克兰官员表示，这些限制束缚了乌克兰的手脚，却让俄罗斯可以放手作战。 Perhaps nowhere was that imbalance clearer than in the Russian air assault overnight. The barrage included 39 ballistic missiles, Mr. Zelensky said. That would be the largest such salvo during the entire war, according to a New York Times data set based on Ukrainian Air Force figures. 这种不对等局面在俄罗斯夜间发动的空袭中表现得尤为明显。泽连斯基表示，这轮袭击包括39枚弹道导弹。根据《纽约时报》依据乌克兰空军数据建立的数据集，这是整场战争期间规模最大的一次弹道导弹齐射。 Even as Russia pounds Ukraine day after day, leading to some of the highest civilian death tolls seen in years of war, Kyiv says it is abiding by Mr. Trump’s demand not to strike Russian oil refineries. Its campaign against refineries, which had led to fuel shortages across Russia, made Russians feel the war as never before . 尽管俄罗斯日复一日地猛烈轰炸乌克兰，造成多年来最严重的平民伤亡，基辅表示，自己仍在遵守特朗普停止袭击俄罗斯炼油厂的要求。此前，乌克兰针对炼油厂的袭击行动导致俄罗斯各地出现燃料短缺，让俄罗斯民众 以前所未有的程度感受到战争的影响 。 Kyiv has said it is unfair that Russia is still attacking Ukraine’s power plants and substations. Mr. Zelensky has asserted that the strikes violate Mr. Trump’s self-declared energy cease-fire in Ukraine. The Trump administration views the cease-fire as covering only strikes on oil refineries, even though Ukraine has none that are operational. 基辅表示，俄罗斯仍在袭击乌克兰的发电厂和变电站，这有失公平。泽连斯基坚称，这些袭击违反了特朗普自行宣布的乌克兰能源停火安排。特朗普政府则认为，这项停火安排仅涵盖针对炼油厂的袭击，尽管乌克兰目前并没有仍在运营的炼油厂。 救援人员正在转移一名在基辅公寓楼袭击中受伤的居民。 Ukraine has set aside its most potent tool against Russia in part because it is worried that Mr. Trump could follow through on an apparent threat to stop providing intelligence that Kyiv needs to warn its people of incoming Russian strikes. 乌克兰搁置了它对付俄罗斯最有力的手段，部分原因是担心特朗普可能兑现其停止提供情报的威胁。基辅需要这些情报，才能向民众预警俄罗斯即将发动的袭击。 While Ukraine’s European partners have so far stepped in to patch Ukraine’s ballooning budget gaps as Russia batters the Ukrainian economy, Europe is not believed to be able to fully fill intelligence deficits if the United States were to pull back. 在俄罗斯持续打击乌克兰经济之际，乌克兰的欧洲伙伴一直在帮助填补该国不断扩大的预算缺口。但外界普遍认为，如果美国撤出，欧洲将无法完全弥补由此产生的缺口。 Ukrainian fears have been elevated over the past two days as Mr. Zelensky has reported that Ukraine did not receive early warnings about Russian missile strikes, though Mr. Trump said on Tuesday that intelligence was still being shared. 过去两天 ，乌克兰的担忧进一步加剧。泽连斯基报告称，乌方没有收到俄罗斯导弹袭击的预警，尽管特朗普周二表示，美国仍在与乌克兰分享情报。 The Ukrainian Air Force clarified on Wednesday that while it had received no advance warning before a Russian missile struck at about 10:40 p.m. on Tuesday, it did receive warnings related to three subsequent waves of attacks that night. Such intelligence sharing is separate from Ukraine’s use of the Starshield system. 乌克兰空军周三 澄清 说，虽然周二晚间10时40分左右，一枚俄罗斯导弹来袭前，乌方没有收到提前预警，但对于当晚随后发生的三波袭击，乌方确实收到了预警。这类情报共享与乌克兰使用星盾系统是两回事。 The Starshield limitations, if they continue, could hobble Ukraine’s military operations. Starshield terminals are used for nearly everything the Ukrainian Army deploys on the battlefield: the cars that carry troops and matériel, the drones that ferry food and water to soldiers at the front, and the attack drones that fly long distances to hit Russian positions. 如果星盾的使用限制持续下去，乌克兰的军事行动可能受到严重阻碍。从运送部队和物资的车辆，到向前线士兵运送食物和饮水的无人机，再到远程飞行打击俄军阵地的攻击无人机，乌军投入战场的几乎所有装备都要用到星盾终端。 The Ukrainian military uses thousands of terminals connected to Starshield, a version of the Starlink network that is harder to hack or jam. Mr. Musk said earlier this year that Starshield was “operated by the U.S. government.” 乌克兰军方使用数以千计与星盾相连的终端。星盾是星链网络的一个版本，更难被黑客攻击或干扰。马斯克今年早些时候 说过 ，星盾由“美国政府运营”。 2023年，乌克兰顿涅茨克地区东部前线附近，一台经过伪装的星链天线。乌克兰军方使用该系统，部分用于引导其不断壮大的无人机机群。 Sasha Maslov for The New York Times Officials from Ukraine’s defense ministry said on Wednesday that, without warning, SpaceX had restricted the use of Starshield for devices traveling faster than 100 miles per hour. When the device exceeded this speed, the terminals lost connection. The officials said the ministry was in touch with the U.S. government, SpaceX and NATO partners to address the issue. 乌克兰国防部官员周三表示，SpaceX在没有事先发出任何通知的情况下，限制了星盾在移动速度超过每小时100英里（约160公里）设备上的使用。一旦设备超过这一速度，终端就会断开连接。官员们说，国防部正在与美国政府、SpaceX和北约伙伴联系，以解决这个问题。 Ukrainian soldiers said missions had been disrupted as a result. Oleksandr, an officer in the 8th Air Assault Corps, said the restrictions had mainly affected heavy bomber and fixed-wing drones targeting Russian logistical routes and positions in occupied territory. He spoke on the condition that he be identified by only his first name, in keeping with Ukrainian military rules. 乌克兰士兵表示，相关限制已经干扰了作战任务。第八空中突击军军官亚历山大说，受影响的主要是重型轰炸无人机和固定翼无人机的作战行动。这些无人机用于打击俄罗斯在乌克兰占领区的后勤补给线和军事阵地。出于乌克兰军方规定，他只允许透露名字。 Oleksandr said that if the restrictions remained in effect, Russia would be able to reopen crucial supply routes in a matter of days, and could better protect expensive equipment, including ships, from Ukrainian attacks. 亚历山大表示，如果这些限制继续实施，俄罗斯将在几天内重新打通关键补给路线，并能更有效地保护包括舰船在内的昂贵装备，免遭乌克兰的袭击。 Starshield also provides connections to the interceptor drones that Ukraine uses to shoot down the Russian attack drones known as Shaheds, especially the fast-flying jet-powered models that Russia is now launching toward Ukraine en masse, said Mr. Beskrestnov, the military-technology adviser to Mr. Zelensky. 泽连斯基的军事技术顾问别斯克列斯特诺夫表示，星盾还为乌克兰用于击落俄罗斯“见证者”攻击无人机的拦截无人机提供通信连接，特别是在应对俄罗斯如今大规模发射、 飞行速度极快的喷气动力型号 时。 “In effect, our partners’ actions are depriving us of one of the few ways we have to defend the country against jet-powered Shaheds,” Mr. Beskrestnov said. “实际上，我们的伙伴正在通过这些行动剥夺我们保卫国家、抵御喷气动力‘见证者’无人机的为数不多的手段之一，”别斯克列斯特诺夫说。 Ryan Mac、Carlotta Gall、Siobhán O’Grady和Maria Varenikova对本文有报道贡献。 Constant Méheut 是时报记者，报道乌克兰战争。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 老龄化的欧洲，愤怒的年轻人
description: KATRIN BENNHOLD2026年10月15日周二在法国波尔多发生的一场学生抗议活动。 Christophe Archambault/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Over the last few years we’ve seen the rise of a formidable political force: Gen Z protesters. They have toppled governments in Bangladesh, Nepal, Peru and Madagascar. They’re behind India’s largest protests in years, which so far have forced the resignation of the country’s education minister. 过去几年中，我们见证了一股强大政治力量的崛起：Z世代抗议者。他们推翻了孟加拉国、尼泊尔、秘鲁和马达加斯加的政府。他们是印度近年来最大规模抗议活动的幕后推手，这些抗议迄今已迫使该国教育部长辞职。 Now we’re witnessing protests by young people in France, who share the anger of other Gen Z protesters around the world, but not the same political power. Because unlike their contemporaries outside the West, young people in Europe are a shrinking demographic. Today my colleague Amanda Taub writes about the intense generational tensions in the West’s aging societies and why they risk becoming a vicious cycle. 如今，我们正目睹法国年轻人的抗议活动，他们与世界各地其他Z世代抗议者有着共同的愤怒，却不具备相同的政治力量。因为与西方以外的同龄人不同，欧洲的年轻人是一个正在萎缩的人口群体。今天，我的同事阿曼达·陶布撰文探讨了西方老龄化社会中激烈的世代紧张局势，以及为什么这些局势有着演变成恶性循环的风险。 A zero-sum game 零和博弈 By Amanda Taub 文/阿曼达·陶布 France may seem like a nation of perpetual protest. But if you are trying to make sense of the latest wave of demonstrations spurred on by young people angry over dilapidated schools, it might help to cast your mind back just a few years. 法国似乎是一个永远处于抗议之中的国家。但若想理解这波由年轻人对学校设施破败的愤怒引发的最新示威浪潮，回想一下几年前的情况可能会有所帮助。 Not long ago, the French took to the streets when President Emmanuel Macron raised the retirement age from 62 to 64. The outcry was so intense that the government eventually suspended the measure; France’s pensions remain one of the biggest drains on the budget of a nation with one of the highest debt levels in Europe. 不久前，当总统马克龙将退休年龄从62岁提高到64岁时，法国人走上了街头。强烈呼声如此剧烈，以至于政府最终暂停了该措施；对于这个债务水平居欧洲前列的国家而言，法国的养老金仍然是国家预算中最大的负担之一。 Today’s protesters have taken to the barricades to demand more resources for the young, while the earlier ones marched to protect resources for the old. In both cases, the protesters saw themselves in a fight with the French government; it might be equally valid to say they were — and still are — in a fight with each other. 今天的抗议者走上街头，是为了要求为年轻人提供更多资源，此前的抗议者游行则是为了保护老年人的资源。在这两种情况下，抗议者都认为自己是在与法国政府斗争；但同样可以说，他们过去和现在，都是在彼此对抗。 The dissatisfaction currently roiling Europe, from France to Spain to Britain to Belgium, is about many things: schools, housing, pensions, unemployment. But step back, and it’s also about one big thing — a generational fight over an economic pie fixed in its size by the continent’s chronic slow economic growth. 从法国到西班牙，从英国到比利时，目前席卷欧洲的不满情绪涉及许多方面：学校、住房、养老金、失业。但退一步来看，这也是一场关于一个大问题的争斗——一场围绕经济蛋糕的代际之争，而蛋糕的大小已因欧洲长期低迷的经济增长而固定不变。 ‘Gerontonomia’ “老龄治理” As Europe’s population ages, conflict may be unavoidable. Because ultimately, different generations have different economic interests, said Tim Vlandas, a professor at Oxford. 随着欧洲人口老龄化，冲突可能是不可避免的。牛津大学教授蒂姆·弗兰达斯指出，归根结底，不同的世代拥有不同的经济利益。 Young people need investments in education, a strong labor market and affordable housing. People over 65, by contrast, tend to want generous pensions and social care, protection for the value of their homes and other assets, and low inflation, even at the cost of higher unemployment. (No one likes inflation, but retirees who rely on savings and fixed incomes are particularly sensitive to it.) 年轻人需要对教育的投资、强劲的劳动力市场和负担得起的住房。相比之下，65岁以上的人群往往希望获得丰厚的养老金和社会护理，希望其房产及其他资产的价值得到保障，并希望通胀率保持较低水平，即使这意味着失业率会上升。（没有人喜欢通胀，但依赖储蓄和固定收入的退休人员对此尤为敏感。） As older people become a larger portion of the population in aging societies, their political influence has also grown, and they have been getting their way. The result is what Vlandas calls “gerontonomia,” a form of “democratically sustained economic stagnation.” 随着老年人在老龄化社会中占总人口的比例越来越大，他们的政治影响力也随之增长，并且逐渐如愿以偿。其结果就是弗兰达斯所说的“老龄治理”，一种“由民主维持的经济停滞”形式。 The disease and its symptoms are widespread. In France, youth unemployment stands at around 20 percent. GDP growth fell to zero percent in the second quarter of this year. Pension costs make up approximately a quarter of all public spending, in part because the retirement age is so low, but there is little political appetite for changing it. Many, particularly on the left, have argued that it is possible to preserve pensions and increase education spending. But the question of how to pay remains. The looming threat of a debt crisis makes further borrowing difficult. And wealth taxes, while often politically appealing, have not raised much money in the past. 这种疾病及其症状非常普遍。在法国，青年失业率保持在20%左右。今年第二季度GDP增长降至零。养老金成本约占所有公共支出的四分之一，部分原因是退休年龄太低，但在政治上几乎没有改变它的意愿。许多人——尤其是左翼人士——主张既可以保留养老金，又可以增加教育支出。但资金来源的问题依然存在。迫在眉睫的债务危机威胁使得进一步借贷变得困难。而财富税虽然在政治上常常具有吸引力，但在过去并没有筹集到多少资金。 87岁的退休老人玛丽卡门·阿巴斯卡尔，她被驱逐出家门一事在西班牙引发了全国范围的抗议活动。 Oscar Del Pozo/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images The situation is similar in Spain, which has one of the oldest populations in Europe, and where protests over a housing crisis recently contributed to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s decision to call new elections. While the face of the protests was an 87-year-old renter, many young people joined, because the housing crisis disproportionately affects them. 西班牙的情况也类似，该国是欧洲人口老龄化最严重的国家之一，最近针对住房危机的抗议活动促使首相桑切斯决定举行新的大选。虽然抗议活动的代表人物是一位87岁的租户，但许多年轻人也加入其中，因为住房危机对他们的影响尤为严重。 Spanish youth unemployment is over 22 percent. House prices have risen far more quickly than wages, adding to the wealth of older generations, but leaving many young people with a choice of living with their parents well into their 30s or sacrificing savings to pay a steep rent. 西班牙的青年失业率超过22%。房价上涨速度远快于工资增长，增加了年长一代的财富，却让许多年轻人面临选择：要么30多岁了还要和父母同住，要么牺牲储蓄去支付高昂的租金。 In Britain, the youth unemployment rate is lower, around 16 percent. But housing costs are steep, particularly in and around London, where most job growth is located. And the country has committed to the so-called “triple lock,” a policy that has for years ensured pensions have risen faster than wages. 在英国，青年失业率较低，约为16%。但住房成本高昂，尤其是在大部分就业增长所在的伦敦及其周边地区。此外，该国还承诺实行所谓的“三重保障”政策，该政策多年来一直确保养老金的涨幅高于工资的涨幅。 In a recent speech, Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to overhaul the policy, long considered untouchable. One union leader called the pledge “almost electoral insanity,” even though Burnham promised to spend the money saved on adult social care, which would largely benefit the aged, too. 在最近的一次演讲中，首相伯纳姆承诺改革这项长期以来被视为不可触碰的政策。一位工会领导人称这一承诺“几乎是选举上的疯狂行为”，尽管伯纳姆承诺将省下来的资金用于成人社会护理，而这大部分也将让老年人受益。 昨天，巴黎举行了一场要求实行与通胀挂钩的养老金的抗议活动。 Mehdi Fedouach/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Why older people have an edge 为何老年人占据优势 Wealthy nations can look forward to more of these battles, but older people may continue to set the political agenda. 可以预见，富裕国家未来还会有更多这样的斗争，但老年人或将继续主导政治议程。 The elderly are well-placed to rally others to their cause, because they have institutions on their side, said Kevin Arceneaux, a political science professor at Sciences Po in Paris. Political parties and unions have an incentive to protect the interests of older people, who make up the bulk of their membership and voting coalitions. 巴黎政治学院的政治学教授凯文·阿塞诺表示，老年人非常擅长团结其他人支持他们的主张，因为他们有体制作为后盾。政党和工会有动力去保护老年人的利益，因为老年人构成了其成员和投票联盟的主体。 It is also easier to convince young people to support old-age benefits that they might one day receive than it is to convince old people to pay more for education that they will never use themselves. Younger generations share some of the benefits from spending on the elderly, experts say. Adult children still living at home may see pension payments as part of their household’s income, rather than a transfer from young workers to retirees. 此外，相比说服老年人为他们自己永远用不到的教育多掏钱，说服年轻人支持他们有朝一日可能领取的晚年福利也要容易得多。专家表示，年轻一代能分享到针对老年人支出的一些好处。仍与父母同住的成年子女可能会将养老金视为其家庭收入的一部分，而非年轻劳动者向退休人员转移的资金。 In Britain, Laura Serra, a researcher at the London School of Economics, has found that working-age generations often worry they will have to support their aging parents themselves if pensions are cut. In fact, France’s young people were out in force to support the 2023 protests against Macron’s proposed pension reform. 在英国，伦敦政治经济学院的研究员劳拉·塞拉发现，适龄劳动力世代常常担心，如果养老金被削减，他们将不得不亲自赡养老龄父母。事实上，法国的年轻人曾大举出动，支持2023年反对马克龙提出的养老金改革方案的抗议活动。 But with economic growth slow in much of the continent, and government borrowing becoming prohibitively expensive, choices may have to be made. And when they are, young people, and perhaps economies as a whole, will be at a disadvantage. 然而，由于欧洲大部分地区的经济增长缓慢，且政府借贷变得昂贵至极，人们可能不得不做出选择。一旦做出选择时，年轻人——甚至可能是整个经济体——将处于不利地位。 Last week, as young people blocked schools across the country, France’s lawmakers met to review next year’s budget. One of their first moves was to preserve a tax break for pensioners. 上周，就在年轻人封锁全国各地的学校时，法国议员们正开会审查明年的预算。他们的首批举措之一就是保留针对退休人员的税收优惠政策。 本文节译自时报全球新闻电邮The World。 翻译：晋其角
content: KATRIN BENNHOLD 2026年10月15日 周二在法国波尔多发生的一场学生抗议活动。 Christophe Archambault/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Over the last few years we’ve seen the rise of a formidable political force: Gen Z protesters. They have toppled governments in Bangladesh, Nepal, Peru and Madagascar. They’re behind India’s largest protests in years, which so far have forced the resignation of the country’s education minister. 过去几年中，我们见证了一股强大政治力量的崛起：Z世代抗议者。他们推翻了孟加拉国、尼泊尔、秘鲁和马达加斯加的政府。他们是印度近年来最大规模抗议活动的幕后推手，这些抗议迄今已迫使该国教育部长辞职。 Now we’re witnessing protests by young people in France, who share the anger of other Gen Z protesters around the world, but not the same political power. Because unlike their contemporaries outside the West, young people in Europe are a shrinking demographic. Today my colleague Amanda Taub writes about the intense generational tensions in the West’s aging societies and why they risk becoming a vicious cycle. 如今，我们正目睹法国年轻人的抗议活动，他们与世界各地其他Z世代抗议者有着共同的愤怒，却不具备相同的政治力量。因为与西方以外的同龄人不同，欧洲的年轻人是一个正在萎缩的人口群体。今天，我的同事阿曼达·陶布撰文探讨了西方老龄化社会中激烈的世代紧张局势，以及为什么这些局势有着演变成恶性循环的风险。 A zero-sum game 零和博弈 By Amanda Taub 文/阿曼达·陶布 France may seem like a nation of perpetual protest. But if you are trying to make sense of the latest wave of demonstrations spurred on by young people angry over dilapidated schools, it might help to cast your mind back just a few years. 法国似乎是一个永远处于抗议之中的国家。但若想理解这波由年轻人对学校设施破败的愤怒引发的最新示威浪潮，回想一下几年前的情况可能会有所帮助。 Not long ago, the French took to the streets when President Emmanuel Macron raised the retirement age from 62 to 64. The outcry was so intense that the government eventually suspended the measure; France’s pensions remain one of the biggest drains on the budget of a nation with one of the highest debt levels in Europe. 不久前，当总统马克龙将退休年龄从62岁提高到64岁时， 法国人走上了街头 。强烈呼声如此剧烈，以至于政府最终暂停了该措施；对于这个债务水平居欧洲前列的国家而言，法国的养老金仍然是国家预算中最大的负担之一。 Today’s protesters have taken to the barricades to demand more resources for the young, while the earlier ones marched to protect resources for the old. In both cases, the protesters saw themselves in a fight with the French government; it might be equally valid to say they were — and still are — in a fight with each other. 今天的抗议者走上街头，是为了要求为年轻人提供更多资源，此前的抗议者游行则是为了保护老年人的资源。在这两种情况下，抗议者都认为自己是在与法国政府斗争；但同样可以说，他们过去和现在，都是在彼此对抗。 The dissatisfaction currently roiling Europe, from France to Spain to Britain to Belgium, is about many things: schools, housing, pensions, unemployment. But step back, and it’s also about one big thing — a generational fight over an economic pie fixed in its size by the continent’s chronic slow economic growth. 从法国到西班牙，从英国到比利时，目前席卷欧洲的不满情绪涉及许多方面：学校、住房、养老金、失业。但退一步来看，这也是一场关于一个大问题的争斗——一场围绕经济蛋糕的代际之争，而蛋糕的大小已因欧洲长期低迷的经济增长而固定不变。 ‘Gerontonomia’ “老龄治理” As Europe’s population ages, conflict may be unavoidable. People over 65, by contrast, tend to want generous pensions and social care, protection for the value of their homes and other assets, and low inflation, even at the cost of higher unemployment. Many, particularly on the left, have argued that it is possible to preserve pensions and increase education spending. But the question of how to pay remains. The looming threat of a debt crisis makes further borrowing difficult. House prices have risen far more quickly than wages, adding to the wealth of older generations, but leaving many young people with a choice of living with their parents well into their 30s or sacrificing savings to pay a steep rent. 西班牙的青年失业率超过22%。房价上涨速度远快于工资增长，增加了年长一代的财富，却让许多年轻人面临选择：要么30多岁了还要和父母同住，要么牺牲储蓄去支付高昂的租金。 In Britain, the youth unemployment rate is lower, around 16 percent. But housing costs are steep, particularly in and around London, where most job growth is located. And the country has committed to the so-called “triple lock,” a policy that has for years ensured pensions have risen faster than wages. 在英国，青年失业率较低，约为16%。但住房成本高昂，尤其是在大部分就业增长所在的伦敦及其周边地区。此外，该国还承诺实行所谓的“三重保障”政策，该政策多年来一直确保养老金的涨幅高于工资的涨幅。 In a recent speech, Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged to overhaul the policy , long considered untouchable. One union leader called the pledge “almost electoral insanity,” even though Burnham promised to spend the money saved on adult social care, which would largely benefit the aged, too. 在最近的一次演讲中，首相伯纳姆 承诺改革 这项长期以来被视为不可触碰的政策。一位工会领导人称这一承诺“几乎是选举上的疯狂行为”，尽管伯纳姆承诺将省下来的资金用于成人社会护理，而这大部分也将让老年人受益。 昨天，巴黎举行了一场要求实行与通胀挂钩的养老金的抗议活动。 Mehdi Fedouach/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images Why older people have an edge 为何老年人占据优势 Wealthy nations can look forward to more of these battles, but older people may continue to set the political agenda. 可以预见，富裕国家未来还会有更多这样的斗争，但老年人或将继续主导政治议程。 The elderly are well-placed to rally others to their cause, because they have institutions on their side, said Kevin Arceneaux, a political science professor at Sciences Po in Paris. title: 新任白宫新闻秘书在中国做过律师吗？我们进行了事实核查
description: SHAWN McCREESH2026年10月15日 Is President Trump’s new press secretary a lawyer — or did she just play one on TV? 特朗普总统的新任新闻秘书是一名真正的律师，还是只是在电视上演过律师？ Three days into her job, Katie Zacharia is facing questions about whether she has embroidered her credentials. She describes herself as a lawyer, and the president called her “an attorney.” When she was asked on Tuesday in which state she passed the bar exam, she twice replied, “When I moved to China.” 上任仅三天，凯蒂·扎卡里亚便面临了履历造假的质疑。她自称是lawyer（律师），而总统则称其为“an attorney”（一位执业律师）。周二，当被问及她在哪个州通过了律师资格考试时，她两次回答称：“我搬去中国的时候。” Huh? 啊？ The moment capped off a shaky debut for the woman who has accepted what is perhaps the most challenging public relations post in the United States. Now she was struggling to tell her own story. 对这位接下了或许是全美最具挑战性的公关职位的女性而言，这一幕为她波折不断的首次亮相画上了句点。如今，她正竭力把自己的经历讲圆。 On Wednesday evening, she told The New York Times that this whole mishegas over “lawyer,” “attorney,” and “China,” has been one big misunderstanding. 周三晚间，她对《纽约时报》表示，围绕“lawyer”、“attorney”与“中国”的这场纷扰完全是一场大误会。 “I assumed the question was, ‘Where were you after law school?’” she said, taking a quick phone call on the tarmac in Arizona, where the president was holding a midterm rally. “我当时以为问题是：‘你从法学院毕业后去了哪里？’”她说。当时总统正在亚利桑那州举行中期选举集会，她是在停机坪上匆匆接通电话时作出这番回应的。 “That’s all I could hear over the sound of Marine One,” she said. “And, wanting to respect protocol, the distance behind the president, kept me from moving closer to hear the question.” “在‘海军陆战队一号’的噪音下，我只能听清这些，”她说.“而且出于遵守礼宾规程的考虑，我与总统保持着一定距离，这让我无法靠前听清问题。” It was only her second day on the job, she pointed out. 她强调，那天只是她履新的第二天。 So here’s the truth about Katie Zacharia, not-quite attorney-at-law: She graduated with a law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011. That technically makes her a lawyer. But is she an attorney, someone who is licensed to practice law and give legal advice? For that, she would have needed to pass the bar. The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that she sat for the California bar exam after graduating law school, but didn’t pass. The Times was unable to find a law license for her in California, or anywhere else she has lived in the United States. 那么，关于这位算不上真正的“attorney”的凯蒂·扎卡里亚，事实究竟是怎样的：她于2011年毕业于佩珀代因大学并获法学学位。严格意义上讲，这确实使她成了一名“lawyer”。但她是否是一名拥有执业许可、能够提供法律咨询的“attorney”？若想具备这一资格，她必须通过律师资格考试。《华尔街日报》周三报道称，她在法学院毕业后曾参加加州律师资格考试，但并未通过。《纽约时报》也未能在加州或她在美居住过的任何其他地方查到其律师执业执照。 During the brief phone call Wednesday, The Times did not get a chance to press her again about whether she had ever passed a bar exam. But before she had to go, she did explain that when she first began appearing on cable news, she consulted with Pepperdine’s president as to how she should identify herself. She said she was warned not to use the words “attorney” or “esquire,” but that “lawyer” was OK. 在周三那通简短的通话中，《纽约时报》未能再次追问她是否曾通过任何律师资格考试。但在挂断前，她确实解释称，当初刚开始在有线电视新闻亮相时，她曾就该如何标明自己的身份咨询过佩珀代因大学校长。她表示，当时对方告诫她不要使用“attorney”或“esquire”这类称谓，但表示使用“lawyer”没有问题。 But what about “general counsel,” would that be OK? Because, on LinkedIn, Ms. Zacharia identified herself as such for Fix California, a group led by Trump loyalist Richard Grenell. 但使用“总法律顾问”(general counsel)又是否合规呢？因为在领英上，扎卡里亚在特朗普亲信理查德·格雷内尔领导的团体“修复加州”名下，将自己的职务标注为总法律顾问。 “You can’t be a general counsel to a company in the United States unless you’re admitted to the bar to practice law,” said Erwin Chemerinsky, the dean of the law school at the University of California, Berkeley. “A general counsel implies that you’re practicing law, giving legal advice to the company. You can’t practice law without a license.” “在美国，你要获得律师资格并获准执业，否则不得担任企业的总法律顾问，”加州大学伯克利分校法学院院长埃尔温·切梅林斯基指出，“‘总法律顾问’意味着你正在从事法律执业工作，正在为企业提供法律建议。没有执照是不得从事法律执业的。” On Wednesday, a watchdog group filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association, calling for an investigation into whether Ms. Zacharia “repeatedly held herself out to the public as entitled to practice law without a license to do so, conduct California law treats as a crime.” 周三，一家监督机构向加州律师公会递交申诉，要求调查扎卡里亚是否存在“在未获执照的情况下，屡次向公众声称自己有法律执业资质，而加州法律将这种行为视为犯罪”。 And that brings us to China. 这就牵涉到了中国之行。 The White House explained this week that Ms. Zacharia moved to China with her husband, Tyler, who had a job at a U.S. private equity firm. While there, she worked on “international transaction law,” Ms. Zacharia has claimed. 白宫本周解释称，扎卡里亚是随丈夫泰勒前往中国的，后者当时在一家美国私募股权机构任职。扎卡里亚声称，在中国期间，她从事的是“国际交易法”业务。 On her LinkedIn profile, she listed nearly two years of employment at Zhong Lun Law Firm, which is one of China’s biggest law firms, with headquarters in Beijing and offices in Tokyo, New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco and Almaty, Kazakhstan. 在其领英个人主页上，她列出了在中伦律师事务所近两年的工作经历。中伦是中国最大的律师事务所之一，总部设在北京，并在东京、纽约、洛杉矶、旧金山以及哈萨克斯坦阿拉木图设有分所。 The law firm did not respond to a request for comment on Wednesday. 该律所周三未回应置评请求。 Opportunities for foreign lawyers in China are extremely narrow. Foreign nationals cannot sit for China’s bar exam, hold a Chinese lawyer’s license or advise on Chinese law. They can, however, be hired by Chinese law firms to work on cross-border deals and to advise on foreign or international law. 外国律师在中国的执业空间极为狭窄。外国公民不得参加中国的司法考试、不得持有中国律师执业执照，也不得就中国法律提供咨询意见。不过，他们可受聘于中国律所参与跨境交易，并就外国法或国际法提供法律意见。 Gary Gao, a partner at Zhong Lun who is based in Shanghai, said the firm often hired foreigners for language assistance and to help Chinese staff understand foreign business culture. 中伦律师事务所常驻上海的合伙人高俊表示，律所经常聘用外籍人员协助语言沟通，并帮助中国员工理解外国商业文化。 “They are not practicing Chinese law at any time,” he said, adding that Ms. Zacharia’s role at the firm would have likely been similar to a paid internship. “他们在任何时候都不具备中国法律执业资格，”他表示，并补充称扎卡里亚在律所的岗位很可能类似于带薪实习。 Sida Liu, a law professor at the University of Hong Kong who specializes in mainland law, said that it is misleading for Ms. Zacharia to describe herself as a former associate at Zhong Lun, because it implies that she was a licensed lawyer in China. 专门研究内地法律的香港大学法学教授刘思达指出，扎卡里亚将自己称为中伦律所前“associate”（律师）具有误导性，因为这暗示了她曾是在中国的持证律师。 “Chinese law firms can hire foreign nationals to work in their mainland offices, but such individuals are not classified as P.R.C. lawyers because P.R.C. lawyer qualification requires P.R.C. citizenship,” Mr. Liu said, referring to the People’s Republic of China. “The title ‘associate’ may therefore be somewhat controversial.” “中国律所可以聘用外籍人士在其内地办公室工作，但这类人员不会被归类为中国律师，因为取得中国律师执业资格必须具备中国国籍，”刘思达说，“因此，使用‘associate’这一头衔可能存在争议。” So what are we to make of all this? 那么，这一切到底说明了什么？ It was Mr. Trump who called Ms. Zacharia an “attorney,” and she certainly never corrected the record. She called herself “general counsel,” which was misleading at best. 特朗普称扎卡里亚为“attorney”，而她显然从未对此进行澄清。她还自称为“总法律顾问”，这至少是一种误导。 Confucius wrote in The Analects that without the trust of the people, the state cannot stand. The same goes for a White House press secretary. It is a job that’s all about credibility. It’s pretty tough to succeed if the public (let alone the fourth estate) feels that it cannot trust what it is being told. 孔子在《论语》中写道：“民无信不立。”对于白宫新闻秘书而言亦是如此。这是一份完全建立在公信力之上的工作。如果公众（更不用说媒体界了）觉得所听到的内容不可信，那就很难做好这项工作。 Kitty Bennett自华盛顿、David Pierson自香港对本文有报道贡献。 Shawn McCreesh是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统及其政府新闻。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: SHAWN McCREESH 2026年10月15日 Is President Trump’s new press secretary a lawyer — or did she just play one on TV? 特朗普总统的新任新闻秘书是一名真正的律师，还是只是在电视上演过律师？ Three days into her job, Katie Zacharia is facing questions about whether she has embroidered her credentials. title: 阴谋、疑团和争议：朴正熙暗杀事件电影加剧韩国文化战争
description: CHOE SANG-HUN2026年10月15日 On Aug. 15, 1974, the South Korean leader Park Chung-hee was delivering an address at Seoul’s National Theater when an assassin charged down an aisle, brandishing a .38-caliber Smith & Wesson. 1974年8月15日，韩国领导人朴正熙正在首尔的国立剧场发表演讲时，一名刺客沿着过道冲上前去，手里挥舞着一把点38口径的史密斯威森手枪。 Shots cracked. Mr. Park ducked behind a bulletproof podium as bodyguards and citizens subdued the gunman. But the first lady, Yook Young-soo, whose gentle public persona had contrasted with her husband’s iron-fisted rule, was hit in the head. After Mr. Park’s dying wife was rushed away, he resumed his speech commemorating the end of Japanese rule to a crowd erupting in cheers. 枪声响起。朴正熙躲到防弹讲台后面，保镖和现场民众合力制服了枪手。但第一夫人陆英修头部中弹。与丈夫的铁腕统治形成鲜明对比的是，她在公众面前一直以温柔亲切的形象示人。生命垂危的陆英修被紧急送医后，朴正熙继续发表纪念日本殖民统治结束的演讲，现场人群爆发出欢呼声。 The killing has remained a disputed episode, spawning conspiracy theories that the dictator may have secretly orchestrated the attack and the gunman had not acted alone, in echoes of the assassination of President John F. Kennedy. 这起刺杀事件至今仍充满争议，并催生出种种阴谋论，包括这位独裁者可能秘密策划了袭击，以及枪手并非单独行动，这不禁让人联想到肯尼迪总统遇刺事件。 Now, a movie has reignited those controversies by placing the killing squarely within cross hairs of this nation’s fierce contemporary culture war. “The Assassin(s)” has exposed the competing interpretations of a turbulent modern history marked by colonial rule, military dictatorship and a bloody struggle for democracy. 如今，一部电影重新点燃了这些争议，把这起刺杀案直接置于韩国激烈的当代文化战争的风口浪尖。《暗杀者（们）》暴露出韩国社会对其动荡的现代史的不同解读，这段历史包含殖民统治、军事独裁，以及争取民主的血腥斗争。 电影《暗杀者（们）》中的一个场景。这部影片再次引发了争议，让人联想到肯尼迪总统遇刺事件。 Mr. Park, a schoolteacher-turned-general, seized power in a 1961 military coup and ruled until his spy chief gunned him down in 1979. Almost a half-century after his death, he remains a disputed figure in South Korea. Conservatives revere him as the architect of the country’s transformation from postwar poverty into an industrial powerhouse. Progressives emphasize his darker legacy: the kidnapping, torture and execution of dissidents; his rewriting of the constitution to make himself president for life; and his ruthless censorship. 朴正熙原本是一名教师，后来成为将军，1961年通过军事政变夺取政权，一直统治韩国，直到1979年被自己的情报首脑枪杀。近半个世纪过去，他在韩国仍然是一个充满争议的人物。保守派尊崇他，认为他是推动韩国从战后贫困走向工业强国的设计师。进步派则强调他留下的黑暗遗产：绑架、酷刑折磨和处决异见人士；修改宪法，让自己成为终身总统；以及残酷的新闻审查。 Mixing real events with cinematic fiction, “The Assassin(s)” follows a journalist and a police officer struggling to uncover the truth behind the 1974 shooting. They navigate a perilous era where, as the journalist notes, “seeing what you can and writing what you should” carries immense danger. Standing in their way is the feared K.C.I.A., the Korean Central Intelligence Agency. Mirroring real history, the film depicts an agency that dictates headlines, sends thugs armed with two-by-fours into newsrooms and brutally crushes anyone, from defiant reporters to honest cops, who dares to intervene. 《暗杀者（们）》把真实事件与电影虚构结合起来，讲述一名记者和一名警察努力查明1974年枪击案真相的故事。他们身处一个危机四伏的时代，正如片中那名记者所说，在那个年代，“看到自己能看到的，写下自己应该写的”，都要冒着巨大的风险。挡在他们面前的是令人闻风丧胆的韩国中央情报部。影片按照真实历史描绘了这个机构如何操纵新闻标题，派遣手持方木棍棒的打手闯进报社，并残酷镇压任何胆敢干预的人，无论是敢于反抗的记者，还是正直的警察。 Released on Sept. 23, the movie has topped the box office and sold three million tickets as of Sunday. 这部电影于9月23日上映后登上票房榜首，截至周日，已售出300万张电影票。 The film’s creators have denied any political motive, but conservative opposition lawmakers have accused them of distorting history to portray Mr. Park as a coldblooded dictator who orchestrated his wife’s murder for political gain. The backlash has included boycott campaigns against brands endorsed by the cast, including Burger King. 影片主创否认有任何政治动机，但保守派在野党议员指责他们歪曲历史，将朴正熙描绘成一个为了政治利益而策划谋杀妻子的冷血独裁者。反弹还包括抵制剧组演员代言的品牌，其中包括汉堡王。 Right-wing activists picketed the home of lead actor Yoo Hae-jin, demanding a halt to “left-wing propaganda.” Fearing for their safety, the cast withdrew from this month’s prestigious Busan International Film Festival in Korea, and Mr. Yoo received police protection. 右翼活动人士在主演柳海真的住所外举行抗议，要求停止“左翼宣传”。出于安全考虑，演员们退出了本月在韩国举行的釜山国际电影节，柳海真还获得了警方保护。 电影主演柳海真今年9月出席加拿大多伦多国际电影节。他已成为反对《暗杀者（们）》一片的抗议者针对的目标。 Carlos Osorio/Reuters Progressives, who include members of the governing party, have defended the film, condemning the conservative backlash as censorship. They have organized group screenings and traded insults with protesters outside theaters. The Directors Guild of Korea has warned of a threat to the creative freedom driving South Korean cinema’s global success. 包括执政党成员在内的进步派人士为影片辩护，谴责保守派的反弹属于审查。他们组织集体观影，并与在影院外抗议的人互相谩骂。韩国导演协会警告说，这威胁到了推动韩国电影在全球取得成功的创作自由。 “Because it depicts such a momentous episode in our history,” said moviegoer Lee Min-ho, “I wondered which parts were factual, which were dramatized and why so many questions remain unanswered after all these years.” 观众李敏镐（音）说：“因为这部电影描绘了我们历史上如此重大的事件，我很想知道哪些部分是真实的，哪些经过了艺术加工，以及为什么这么多年过去，还有那么多疑问没有答案。” A Japan Connection 与日本的关联 A government investigation after the attack concluded that the assassin, a Japan-born Korean named Mun Se-gwang, had acted on behalf of a pro-North Korean residents’ association in Japan. It said that one of his bullets struck Mr. Park’s podium while another fatally wounded Ms. Yook. 暗杀事件发生后，政府的调查认定：刺客是在日本出生的韩国人文世光，他是受日本一个亲朝侨民团体指使。调查称，他的一颗子弹击中了朴正熙的讲台，另一颗击中了陆英修，带来致命伤。 The assassination attempt came as Mr. Park was under mounting pressure from both anti-government protests against martial law and diplomatic tensions with Japan, which was angered after the K.C.I.A. abducted opposition leader Kim Dae-jung from a Tokyo hotel. 这起暗杀未遂事件发生时，朴正熙正面临越来越大的压力。一方面，反对戒严令的反政府抗议活动不断高涨；另一方面，韩国与日本的外交关系也日趋紧张。此前，韩国中央情报部在东京一家酒店绑架了反对派领袖金大中，激怒了日本。 Ms. Yook’s death stirred public sympathy for Mr. Park, allowing him to link the attack, however tenuously, to Japan. 陆英修之死激起了公众对朴正熙的同情，也让他得以将这起袭击与日本联系起来，尽管这种关联十分牵强。 1974年11月13日，文世光出庭受审。他因枪击导致陆英修死亡被判处死刑。 Kim Chon Kil/Associated Press Mourners wailed as they watched her chrysanthemum-covered hearse move through central Seoul. Men severed their fingers to write anti-Japanese slogans in blood. Crowds stormed the Japanese Embassy, tearing down its flag and setting a car ablaze. Mr. Mun was hanged on Dec. 20, 1974, three days after being convicted of “murder with intent to commit insurrection” and six days shy of his 23rd birthday. 哀悼者在覆盖着菊花的灵车缓缓穿过首尔市中心时痛哭失声。有人砍断手指，用血写下反日标语。人群冲击日本大使馆，扯下使馆旗帜，并点燃了一辆汽车。文世光于1974年12月20日被处以绞刑，此前三天他被判“意图叛乱的谋杀罪”，再过六天，就是他23岁生日。 Yet questions persisted, fueled by the case’s extraordinary circumstances. 然而，这起案件的种种不同寻常之处使疑问始终挥之不去。 Mr. Mun told investigators that he had stolen the pistol from a Japanese police station. He obtained a South Korean visa using a fake Japanese passport, smuggled the weapon through the airports of both countries inside a radio set and entered a presidential event without the required government-issued identification tag. 文世光对调查人员说，那把手枪是他从日本一个派出所偷来的。他用伪造的日本护照取得了韩国签证，把枪藏在一台收音机里，蒙混过了两国的机场，并在没有政府签发的必要身份识别证件的情况下进入总统出席的活动现场。 Missing Bullets? 消失的子弹？ Investigators said seven shots were heard that day, but not all have been fully accounted for. Officials said Mr. Mun fired four rounds and that a presidential bodyguard also shot, killing a high school student in the audience. At trial, Mr. Mun denied firing at Ms. Yook. The bullet that killed her has never been made public, and no ballistic test of it is known to exist. Under Mr. Park’s grip on the flow of information, the official account stood despite those gaps. 调查人员称，当天现场共响起七声枪响，但并没有找到所有子弹的去向。官员称，文世光开了四枪，一名总统保镖也开了枪，打死了观众席上的一名高中生。审判期间，文世光否认自己向陆英修开枪。导致她死亡的子弹从未对外公布，也没有已知的弹道检测记录。在朴正熙严密控制信息传播的情况下，尽管存在这些疑点，官方说法依然被奉为定论。 In 1989, a retired police forensics officer, Lee Geun-woo, testified that Mr. Park’s presidential security service had removed bullets from the scene before his team reached the theater. He doubted that any of Mr. Mun’s rounds had killed Ms. Yook. 1989年，退休的警方鉴证人员李根宇（音）作证称，在他的团队抵达剧场之前，朴正熙的总统警卫机构已经从现场取走了子弹。他怀疑陆英修并非死于文世光射出的子弹。 Hur Jin-ho, the movie’s director, said that television programs in the early 2000s, which explored unanswered questions about the shooting, led him to believe there may have been more than one assassin. “That’s why I put the ‘s’ in parentheses in the film’s title,” he said. 影片导演许秦豪表示，2000年代初的一些电视节目探讨了这起枪击案尚未解开的疑团，让他开始相信，刺客可能不止一人。“所以我在电影英文片名中把表示复数的字母‘s’放进了括号里，”他说。 导演许秦豪今年9月在多伦多。他表示，自己受到有关这起枪击事件的电视节目的启发。 Carlos Osorio/Reuters His film does not identify Ms. Yook’s killer, but through its characters it challenges the official narrative: Did Mr. Mun have an accomplice? Was a second gunman targeting Ms. Yook while Mr. Mun served as a pawn? Could Mr. Park have been involved in a plot that led to her death? 影片没有指出究竟是谁杀害了陆英修，但通过片中人物对官方说法提出了质疑：文世光是否有同伙？他是否只是一枚棋子，另有一名枪手以陆英修为目标？朴正熙是否可能参与了一场最终导致妻子丧命的阴谋？ The controversy surrounding the film reflects a broader political struggle over how South Koreans remembered their history. 围绕这部电影的争议折射出韩国社会在如何看待和解读本国历史的问题上更广泛的政治角力。 Left-leaning governments have passed laws criminalizing “false” narratives about two events of particular significance to progressives: the 1980 military massacre of pro-democracy demonstrators in the city of Gwangju and the suffering of Korean “comfort women,” who were forced into sexual slavery by Japan’s military during World War II. 左倾政府曾通过法律，将散布有关两起历史事件的“虚假”说法定为犯罪（这两起事件对进步派而言具有特殊意义）。一是1980年军方在光州屠杀支持民主的示威者，二是“二战”期间被日本军队强迫充当性奴隶的韩国“慰安妇”所遭受的苦难。 In recent years, some on the political right have portrayed the comfort women as prostitutes and the Gwangju uprising as a “riot” instigated by North Korea. The right-wing attacks on “The Assassin(s)” are part of a broader backlash against what conservatives see as progressive attempts to dictate how history is told. 近年来，部分右翼人士将慰安妇描述为妓女，并把光州起义称为朝鲜煽动的“暴乱”。右翼对《暗杀者（们）》的攻击是保守派更广泛反弹的一部分。他们认为，进步派正试图控制历史的叙述方式。 “It is a horrific hypocrisy to sanctify and protect, through the threat of imprisonment, only the history they have chosen,” said Na Kyung-won, a conservative lawmaker. “只保护并神圣化他们选定的历史，还用监禁相威胁，这是极其可怕的虚伪行径，”保守派议员罗景垣说。 1977年，朴槿惠（左）在首尔与父亲、实行铁腕统治的总统朴正熙交谈。她后来当选韩国总统，但因卷入丑闻遭到弹劾。 Reuters Park Geun-hye, Mr. Park’s daughter who was elected president decades later and impeached over a corruption scandal, has remained silent on the film. Through an aide, however, she released a handwritten letter from her late father. 朴正熙的女儿朴槿惠几十年后当选总统，后来因腐败丑闻遭到弹劾。她一直没有就这部电影公开表态。不过，她通过一名助手公布了已故父亲的一封亲笔信。 “Your mother took the fatal bullet meant for me,” Mr. Park wrote. “I often wonder how much better it would have been had I been the one hit while your mother survived.” 朴正熙在信中写道：“你母亲替我挡下了那颗致命的子弹。我常常想，如果中弹的是我，而你母亲活了下来，该有多好。” Choe Sang-Hun是时报驻首尔首席记者，报道韩国和朝鲜新闻。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

Mr. Park ducked behind a bulletproof podium as bodyguards and citizens subdued the gunman. But the first lady, Yook Young-soo, whose gentle public persona had contrasted with her husband’s iron-fisted rule, was hit in the head. Kennedy. 这起刺杀事件至今仍充满争议，并催生出种种阴谋论，包括这位独裁者可能秘密策划了袭击，以及枪手并非单独行动，这不禁让人联想到 肯尼迪总统遇刺事件 。 Now, a movie has reignited those controversies by placing the killing squarely within cross hairs of this nation’s fierce contemporary culture war. “ The Assassin(s) ” has exposed the competing interpretations of a turbulent modern history marked by colonial rule, military dictatorship and a bloody struggle for democracy. 如今，一部电影重新点燃了这些争议，把这起刺杀案直接置于韩国激烈的当代文化战争的风口浪尖。 《暗杀者（们）》 暴露出韩国社会对其动荡的现代史的不同解读，这段历史包含殖民统治、军事独裁，以及争取民主的血腥斗争。 电影《暗杀者（们）》中的一个场景。这部影片再次引发了争议，让人联想到肯尼迪总统遇刺事件。 Mr. Park, a schoolteacher-turned-general, seized power in a 1961 military coup and ruled until his spy chief gunned him down in 1979. They navigate a perilous era where, as the journalist notes, “seeing what you can and writing what you should” carries immense danger. Standing in their way is the feared K.C.I.A., the Korean Central Intelligence Agency. He doubted that any of Mr. Mun’s rounds had killed Ms. Yook. 1989年，退休的警方鉴证人员李根宇（音）作证称，在他的团队抵达剧场之前，朴正熙的总统警卫机构已经从现场取走了子弹。他怀疑陆英修并非死于文世光射出的子弹。 Hur Jin-ho, the movie’s director, said that television programs in the early 2000s, which explored unanswered questions about the shooting, led him to believe there may have been more than one assassin. “That’s why I put the ‘s’ in parentheses in the film’s title,” he said. 影片导演许秦豪表示，2000年代初的一些电视节目探讨了这起枪击案尚未解开的疑团，让他开始相信，刺客可能不止一人。“所以我在电影英文片名中把表示复数的字母‘s’放进了括号里，”他说。 导演许秦豪今年9月在多伦多。他表示，自己受到有关这起枪击事件的电视节目的启发。 Carlos Osorio/Reuters His film does not identify Ms. Yook’s killer, but through its characters it challenges the official narrative: Did Mr. Mun have an accomplice? Was a second gunman targeting Ms. Yook while Mr. Mun served as a pawn?
